# TradingLead Desktop - connection and workflow router

Load this before using any TradingLead product command. Read
[commands.md](commands.md) for this skill's exact command fields and native
Desktop controls. Use the installed app's live capabilities as authoritative.

## Connect without exposing credentials

For apps containing managed AI integration, use `tradinglead --help`, then
`tradinglead agent-guide` and `tradinglead skills list`. First launch offers
setup; **Help > AI integrations** enables/repairs the CLI and Copilot skill
registration. Open a new terminal/AI session after setup. No MCP, checkout or
separate Node.js installation is needed for the installed CLI.

If PATH is unavailable, inspect the installed app's `resources/agent/AI-README.md`
(macOS: `Contents/Resources/agent/AI-README.md`) and its adjacent `tradinglead`
or `tradinglead.cmd` helper. The user-local fallback is
`~/.tradinglead-desktop/bin/tradinglead` (`tradinglead.cmd` on Windows).
Do not print `api.json`; the helper handles private discovery.

`tradinglead skills read NAME --file DOCUMENT` reads a listed reference from
the current compatible bundle. `skills status` reports its version, compatibility,
registration conflicts and last update result; `skills update` explicitly checks
the fixed public GitHub source. New skills cannot upgrade native app features.
Older apps without this integration need a Desktop update first.

For **source-checkout development**, the equivalent entry point is
`TradingLead-Desktop/cli.cjs`; the examples below use `tradinglead` from that
repository. Installed users replace `tradinglead` with `tradinglead`.

```bash
tradinglead health
tradinglead tabs
tradinglead desktop status --tab ACTUAL_TAB_ID
tradinglead capabilities --tab ACTUAL_TAB_ID
tradinglead exec workspace.getState --tab ACTUAL_TAB_ID
tradinglead exec chart.getState --tab ACTUAL_TAB_ID
```

1. Check health and tabs. If Desktop is not running, launch the installed app,
   or use the existing repo's documented `npm run dev`. Discover an installed
   bundle from native app metadata, not a guessed path. Do not start a duplicate
   instance, restart an existing app or reload user charts. Change the website
   origin only when the user asks (see the development recipe below).
2. Select the intended native tab. Even with one tab, pass `--tab` explicitly.
   Never choose another tab just because the requested one is unavailable.
3. Check account, chart symbol/feed/interval and permissions before changing
   anything. Readiness does not certify fresh market data.
4. Read that tab's current catalog and the domain capability command before
   authoring code or executing a strategy. Do not invent functions or fields.
5. If not ready, `desktop status` works before workspace registration.
   `desktop reconnect` retries existing access; it cannot grant access.
   `desktop open-access` opens the user control, not an approval bypass.
   Do not reload the page merely to reconnect: unsaved work may exist.

### Troubleshoot an unreachable or stale tab

Newer Desktop builds add `windowCount`, `tabCount` and (only when not ready) a
`hint` to `health`; `tabs` adds a `hint` when it is empty; `desktop status`
adds a `hint` when the tab is not ready. Older builds omit these fields. Follow
the hint; on macOS:

| Symptom | Fix (no app restart) |
| --- | --- |
| Health answers but `tabs` is `[]` / `windowCount:0` (app running with no window) | `open -a TradingLead` reopens a window. |
| `desktop status` shows `page` other than `/charts` (e.g. `/`) | `open "tradinglead://charts"` navigates the **current** tab to charts. |
| On `/charts` but `frontendConnected:false`, or the website was just deployed | Reload via `open "tradinglead://charts"` to load the new frontend build. |

The deep link navigates the active tab, so activate the intended tab first
(`desktop activate --tab ID`) and ask before doing it if the user may have
unsaved work. Then poll `desktop status --tab ID` until `ready:true`.

## Development: point the app at a local dev server

Use this when the user asks, e.g. "point the app to localhost:3001" or "switch
back to production". Run from the TradingLead-Desktop repository.

1. **Check the dev server answers** before switching, or the tab loads an error
   page: `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:3001/charts`
   must print `200` (or a redirect). If not, ask the user to start it.
2. **Read and switch the origin.** The bridge token is the only gate (no AI
   grant, no `--tab`):

   ```bash
   tradinglead desktop getOrigin
   # {origin, cloudOrigin:"https://tradinglead.in", isLocal, allowedOrigins:[...]}
   tradinglead desktop setOrigin --params '{"origin":"http://localhost:3001","path":"/charts"}'
   # {previousOrigin, origin, path, navigated:true, verifyWith}
   ```

   `setOrigin` navigates the **active** tab, so warn the user about unsaved
   work and `desktop activate --tab ID` the intended tab first. Add
   `"navigate":false` to change the origin without loading a page.
3. **Verify.** Poll `tradinglead tabs` until the tab reports `ready:true`.
   The new origin is trusted at once; readiness follows when the dev frontend
   registers. Then run `desktop status --tab ID` (expect the localhost `origin`
   and `page:"/charts"`) and `exec chart.getState --tab ID`. If it stays
   `ready:false`, follow the `desktop status` hint. Page-side AI access
   settings can differ per website origin, so localhost may need the user to enable it
   (`desktop open-access` opens the user's control; agents cannot grant it).
4. **Switch back** when asked or when the dev task ends:
   `tradinglead desktop setOrigin --params '{"origin":"cloud","path":"/charts"}'`,
   then verify with `getOrigin` (`isLocal:false`) and `tabs`.

Allowed origins are only `cloud` / `https://tradinglead.in`,
`https://www.tradinglead.in` and loopback `http(s)://localhost|127.0.0.1|[::1]`
**with an explicit port**. Remote domains, credentials, paths, queries or
fragments in `origin` fail with `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` (403). A bad `path` (it must
start with `/` and contain no scheme or `//`) fails with `INVALID_PATH` (400). After a switch,
requests still in flight on a page that lost trust or navigated end with
`NOT_READY`. Re-check `tabs` and retry with the same idempotency key.

### Diagnostics controls (read-only)

```bash
tradinglead desktop appInfo     # version, electron, buildChannel, isDev, origin, protocol, per-tab catalog
tradinglead desktop services    # feed registry, sidecar (no credentials), Python runtime, updater
tradinglead desktop logs --params '{"kind":"events","tail":50}'   # or kind "bars"; tail 1-200
tradinglead desktop screenshot [--tab TAB_ID] [--params '{"selector":"#chart"}']
```

`screenshot` captures the given tab (default: the active trusted tab; with
several tabs and none active it answers `TAB_REQUIRED`), optionally cropped to
the first visible element matching `selector` (≤256 chars; `INVALID_SELECTOR`,
`SELECTOR_NOT_FOUND`). It writes a private PNG under
`~/.tradinglead-desktop/screenshots/` (newest 50 kept) and returns
`{path, bytes, width, height, tabId}`. `logs` returns redacted, bounded JSON
entries; it never exposes tokens. `appInfo.tabs[].catalog` shows the accepted
entry count, `hash`, `buildId` and the per-entry `rejected` list
(`{type, reason}`, max 64, plus `rejectedCount`). A tab whose catalog had bad
entries is still ready with the valid ones; inspect `rejected` when a command
is unexpectedly `UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND`.

Catalog protocol 2 (`appInfo.protocol`): Desktop validates each entry
independently, ignores unknown descriptor fields, passes `effects`, and accepts
a renderer `aliases` map (≤128). Alias commands such as `simulation.*` are
listed with `aliasOf` and execute with the canonical command's grants and retry
identity. Limits: 256 accepted entries and 128 KiB of minified UTF-8 JSON
(aliases excluded).

The developer-only diag HTTP bridge (`~/.tradinglead-desktop/diag/bridge.json`)
starts only in dev builds or with `TL_DIAG_BRIDGE=1`; it has no script or
devtools routes. Prefer the controls above.

`getOrigin`/`setOrigin` and the diagnostics controls need a Desktop build that
contains them (`desktop capabilities` lists app-level ones under `appActions`).
Older builds answer `INVALID_REQUEST`. On those builds
use the alternatives: press **⌘L** (Ctrl+L) in the app and use its
Local/Cloud switch or type the URL. When launching a dev shell, pass
`--url=http://localhost:3001/charts` or set `ELECTRON_APP_URL`. A runtime switch
(control or ⌘L) overrides the launch URL until the app restarts. Never restart
a running app just to change its origin.

The CLI reads private local discovery itself. Never print the discovery token,
put it in command-line arguments, paste raw diagnostic state, or reuse discovery
across app restarts. Browser-only tabs do not provide this external transport.

Desktop is a hybrid shell: the installed package supplies native IPC, isolation
and transport, while its active origin supplies the frontend catalog and
handlers. A local frontend checkout, the installed shell, the loaded website
and this skill collection can all be different versions. Installing skills
deploys none of them. A ready catalog proves advertised commands, not that every
handler, market feed or saved write succeeds.

If `node install.cjs --check` passes in the canonical skill collection but a
workflow such as `tl-paper-trading` is missing from this agent's available list,
refresh skill discovery or start a new session. Do not create a duplicate skill
or replace a correct link merely to change a cached listing.

## Native clicks, scrolling, typing and recording

**Desktop 0.1.9 or later is required.** Read
[ui-automation.md](ui-automation.md) before input or recording. Check
`tradinglead desktop capabilities` on the actual installation: older shells
cannot acquire these controls through a skill update.

Prefer a domain command for a supported operation. For ordinary UI work without
one, use this **inspect -> one action -> verify** loop:

1. Discover the intended tab, activate it only when appropriate, and check
   `desktop status --tab ID`. Keep that chart tab visible. Do not change feeds,
   accounts or tabs just to make a target accessible.
2. Read native capabilities, then request `desktop ui-enable --tab ID --key KEY`.
   A person must approve the native prompt. Existing write grants are also
   required; agents must never click permission controls or approve themselves.
3. Use `desktop ui-inspect --tab ID` to obtain actual selectors, viewport
   rectangles and `automationScope`. Prefer a unique selector over coordinates.
   Never invent a selector from a screenshot or reuse stale positions.
4. Send one `desktop ui-click`, `ui-hover`, `ui-scroll`, `ui-type` or `ui-key`
   with an explicit tab and a fresh operation key. These are native **desktop**
   actions, not `exec` commands. Right-click uses `"button":"right"`;
   double-click uses `"clickCount":2`. Use `"replace":true` to replace text
   rather than append, and `--params-file` for long text.
5. Inspect again after each action. Scroll the actual nested container in
   modest increments, then inspect again; hover before looking for hover-only
   controls. After opening a menu, discover the new item before clicking it.
   Use bounded polling of the domain state when work is asynchronous, not blind
   rapid clicks or fixed sleep chains.
6. `dispatched:true,verified:false` means input was sent, not that it succeeded
   or saved. Verify through inspection, an authorized screenshot or the relevant
   domain state. An uncertain retry uses the **same key and parameters**;
   a genuinely new action uses a new key. Stop on protected targets or revoked
   consent instead of searching for a bypass.
7. Finish with `desktop ui-disable --tab ID --key KEY`. Consent also expires
   after ten minutes and is revoked by tab/account/navigation/grant changes.

The reference gives exact fields, iframe targeting and recovery codes.
**Desktop 0.1.10+:** session approval covers ordinary controls, including
unmarked dialogs, without per-action prompts. The
0.1.9 shell still asks for additional human confirmation on unmarked controls;
skills alone cannot remove those prompts. Updated native `ui-enable` capability
descriptions explicitly advertise "without per-action prompts".
Login, broker setup, credentials, purchases, AI permissions and
Practice Labs stay human-only. Native OS shortcuts, cross-origin frames, file
pickers, clipboard automation and arbitrary JavaScript are not available.

Recording uses **separate consent**: `desktop record-start`, `record-status` and
`record-stop`. It captures only the selected chart tab to a private, video-only
WebM. The person sees a draggable **Stop & save** panel. Stop and wait for
`state:"completed"` before quitting; keep the returned recording ID and file
path. No microphone, system audio, desktop-wide capture or automatic uploads.

## Demos and screenshots

For demo videos and screenshot decks, use these commands:

- `ui.waitIdle` waits until the app is settled.
- `ui.listTargets` and `ui.getTargetRect` return named element boxes (`data-demo-id`).
- `demo.prepare`, `demo.redact` and `demo.reset` control presentation mode and PII blur.

All of these are ephemeral and need no write grant. In plain browsers, the gated `window.__tlDemo` exposes them on dev or loopback hosts only. See [demos.md](demos.md).

## Command and retry protocol

```bash
tradinglead exec research.list --tab ACTUAL_TAB_ID
tradinglead exec research.create --tab ACTUAL_TAB_ID \
  --params-file report-params.json --key UNIQUE_OPERATION_KEY
tradinglead exec pythonIndicators.apply --tab ACTUAL_TAB_ID \
  --source-file indicator.py --params-file input-params.json --key UNIQUE_OPERATION_KEY
```

`--params-file` is a JSON **parameter object**, not a `{type,params}` envelope.
`--source-file` populates `source`; for research HTML use `html` in a params file.
Do not combine `--params` with `--params-file`.

- All descriptors marked `mutates:true` require a unique retry key. Reuse that
  key and identical parameters only when reconciling the same operation. CLI
  keys are 1-80 letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens.
- `mutates:false` does not mean side-effect-free: commands can open panels,
  navigate a chart, modify tab-local drafts, start jobs or consume query quota.
  Read the exact descriptor before using a read-only audit as execution consent.
- Source descriptors declare `effects`: `navigate`, `panel`, `quota`, `code`,
  `write`, `network`, or exclusive `none`. Effects describe possible consequences,
  not grants. Only `none` promises an observational local read. Network-only reads
  do not reveal or select UI, but still contact services.
  Desktop protocol 2 independently negotiates `catalog.effects` and
  `catalog.aliases`; old shells keep full alias entries and receive no new fields.
  Alias callers retain identical runtime validation and retry identity.
- `symbol.details` without `expanded`, `indices.getState` without `category`,
  and `watchlists.multiView` without `panels` need no write grant or retry key.
  Their explicit change variants, including false/empty values, require both.
- Require the **final** JSON `status:"ok"`. HTTP acceptance, request ID or
  process startup is not completion. Inspect domain states such as `preparing`,
  `running`, `paused`, `completed`, and `valid:false` separately.
- In the current source, `feeds.list` can return final `status:"ok"` with only
  the default feed and `data.discovery.status:"error"` /
  `code:"FEED_DISCOVERY_FAILED"` and a bounded `reason`. No broker was verified. Explicit default
  chart/history commands remain independent of broker discovery; a requested
  broker still fails rather than falling back to default.
- The CLI emits an accepted request ID to stderr. A timeout or cancelled
  transport may leave a persisted write. Inspect before retrying; never issue
  a fresh key automatically after an uncertain write.
- `tradinglead cancel --tab TAB --request REQUEST_ID` cancels a transport
  request. A scan/backtest job has its own domain cancellation command.
- The source bridge deduplicates canonical Backtesting/Optimize and legacy
  simulation/research aliases using the same parameters, ignoring object-key
  ordering but preserving array ordering. Older installed shells may report
  `CONFLICT` when switching spellings; retain the original command, key and
  parameters when reconciling an uncertain operation. These retries are bounded
  caches, not a durable transaction log or a promise of rollback.
- Current source transport caps JSON at 2 MiB; older packaged bridges can have
  stricter limits. Domain limits still apply: scanner rows/columns and exports
  remain separately bounded and paginated. Do not concatenate maximum-sized
  source and parameter payloads and assume they fit.
- Identity comes from the active app session, not a `userId` command parameter.
  Stop and rediscover on account changes.
- Current catalogs retain `permission:"indicators"` for local indicator and
  backtesting changes. Older bridges may omit it: absence is not an access
  grant. Pine errors can include bounded diagnostic locations, runtime stage
  context and optional profiles; generic errors do not expose arbitrary
  native fields. Python apply retains its bounded diagnostic text.
- External Pine save/apply/update and Python save/apply default to visible
  Studio presentation; `showInStudio:false` opts out. Check `data.studio`:
  a presentation error with `operationCompleted:true` does not undo the
  mutation. Preserve its IDs and retry only `indicators.openEditor` after
  resolving the blocker; never recreate an applied instance to reopen its UI.
  Dirty drafts are preserved. Read `indicators.editorState.visible` rather
  than assuming a mounted/embedded editor is visible.

## Read error codes, not messages

Current Desktop bridges forward short, single-line domain messages (for
example which parameter is invalid). Messages that could carry URLs, file
paths, credentials or Python runtime text are replaced with `"Command failed."`;
older packaged bridges always replace them. Act on `code` first and use the
message as detail:

| Code | Meaning and next step |
| --- | --- |
| `INVALID_PARAMS` | Parameters are strict: an unknown key, wrong type or out-of-range value. Reread that exact command's descriptor and send only its listed keys (e.g. `backtesting.run` takes `versionSuffix`, `backtesting.applyStrategy` takes `version`). |
| `CHART_NOT_READY` / `CHART_CHANGED` / `SIMULATION_CONTEXT_CHANGED` | Poll `chart.getState` until `ready:true` on the intended context, then retry with a **new** key. |
| `REVISION_CONFLICT` / `REVISION_REQUIRED` | Reread the item and pass its current revision. |
| `SIMULATION_HISTORY_FULL` | Active-run slots are full. Save to the library or ask before deleting; never delete user runs automatically. |
| `BACKTEST_COMPARISON_INCOMPATIBLE` | The runs differ in sample, mode/state or horizon, or include a legacy Pine re-simulation; see [tl-backtesting](../tl-backtesting/SKILL.md). |
| `STRATEGY_ALREADY_APPLIED` | Older catalogs may refuse replacement: inspect the addressed contract before explicitly removing. Current Apply replaces in place and retains auto-rerun intent. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_FEED` / `UNSUPPORTED_SYMBOL` / `DESKTOP_REQUIRED` | Pick a feed/interval from `feeds.list`; no fallback is chosen for you. |
| `SIGN_IN_REQUIRED` / `AGENT_DISABLED` / `APPROVAL_REQUIRED` | Only the user can resolve these; report and stop. |

`workspace.getActivity` lists recent codes. If the code alone is ambiguous,
ask the user to read the message shown in the app rather than guessing.

Desktop local access is automatic for the active account unless paused.
Mutations marked `permission:"indicators"` (including `studyTemplates.manage`)
use `allowAgentIndicators`; other
mutations use the separate `allowAgentWrites` grant. That includes cloud
watchlists/saved screeners and also saved alerts, chart view/compare/actions,
drawings, layouts, Chart Grid, market panels, drawing-template application and
native `chart.replayControl`; the grant is not limited to cloud writes.
Mutations require an active account; cloud writes require real sign-in.
Agents cannot grant permissions, unpause access, or bypass Python isolation.

## Guided Practice Labs

These synthetic-price lessons are separate from `backtesting.practice` paper
accounts. Practice Labs are intentionally human-operated, with no AI lesson
navigation, coach, completion or reset commands. Do not invent a `practice.*`
namespace or target guessed training scopes. Ordinary product commands operate
the normal account workspace, not the lesson's isolated synthetic runtime.

## Route the task

Choose the outcome owner below, not every skill containing the same language
or command prefix. Connection guidance is shared; companion workflows are
needed only when the request crosses their boundary. A Pine backtest does not
require the Python guide, and direct paper practice does not require a backtest.

| Group | Task | Read/load |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start | Connection, tabs, grants, retries, bottom/right panels, theme, activity | this skill |
| Charting | Chart context, feeds, history, snapshots, replay, view/scale/range, Compare, toolbar actions/screenshot, built-in studies, drawings, drawing templates, split layouts/pane targeting, saved chart layouts, Chart Grid | [tl-charts](../tl-charts/SKILL.md) |
| Markets | Watchlists (Watch grid, lists, rows, view, membership), symbol details, peers, Multi Watchlists, indices, heatmap, Market Intelligence, Futures, universes, raw candles | [tl-markets](../tl-markets/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts | Saved price alerts: list/create/edit/enable/delete, trigger activity | [tl-alerts](../tl-alerts/SKILL.md) |
| Analysis | Unified Scanner, original strategies/SQL, grid analysis/refinement, Scanned History, saved rules | [tl-screening](../tl-screening/SKILL.md) |
| Analysis | Historical Patterns: one ticker across weekdays/IST windows, filters, statistics and dated chart navigation | [tl-patterns](../tl-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Analysis | Write/read/edit saved HTML analysis | [tl-research](../tl-research/SKILL.md) |
| Authoring | TLScript-Pine custom indicators (not Pine strategy chart apply) | [tl-tlscript](../tl-tlscript/SKILL.md) |
| Authoring | Python indicators / strategy authoring | [tl-python](../tl-python/SKILL.md) |
| Strategy | Run/review Python or Pine backtests, applied strategies, presets, saved results, overlays | [tl-backtesting](../tl-backtesting/SKILL.md) |
| Strategy | Sweeps / holdout / walk-forward | [tl-strategy-optimization](../tl-strategy-optimization/SKILL.md) |
| Strategy | Replay-to-trade direct practice / backtest-derived replay / forward paper / simulated orders | [tl-paper-trading](../tl-paper-trading/SKILL.md) |
| Quality | Run or author agent-executed test suites (smoke, per-domain, workflows, visual/LLM-judged) and local unit tests | [tl-testing](../tl-testing/SKILL.md) |

## Workspace shell

```json
{"type":"workspace.getState","params":{}}
```

`workspace.getState` reports account/grant flags, bottom `panels`, right
`sidebar {available, panel, expanded}` and the addressed tab.

**Bottom panels** — `workspace.setPanel` with `peers`, `watchlists` (Multi
Watchlists), `futures`, `backtesting`, `paper-trading`, `intelligence` or
`indicators` (Indicator Studio); `simulation` is a legacy alias. Send
`expanded` explicitly. Backtesting may be docked right, independent of the
bottom tab: pass `dock:"bottom"|"right"` (backtesting only) to place and select
it deterministically; `dock:"right"` fails with `DOCK_UNAVAILABLE` below 720px.
Without `dock`, a right-docked Backtesting only toggles its side panel. The
result's `expected` predicts the state; verify `workspace.getState.panels`
(`bottom:{panel,expanded}` is what the bottom dock shows, `backtesting:{dock,visible}`).

**Right sidebar** — `workspace.openSidebar`:

```json
{"type":"workspace.openSidebar","params":{"panel":"alerts","expanded":true}}
```

Panels: `watchlists` (Watch), `indices`, `heatmap`, `scanner` (Scan), `grid`,
`patterns`, `alerts`, `research`, `dataWindow` (Data), and from **More**
`paperTrading` and `contests`. `expanded` defaults to `true`; `false` collapses
the sidebar. It is `mutates:false` (layout only, no retry key) but changes
visible state. It returns `requested:true,confirmed:false`: poll
`workspace.getState.sidebar` until it shows the panel. `WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE`
means `/charts` is not mounted for the signed-in account in that tab. Many
domain commands (heatmap, indices, Watch grid, Grid, Patterns) only
work while their panel is mounted, so open it first.

**Theme** — `workspace.setTheme {"theme":"light"|"dark"}` changes the
browser-local app theme (Settings > Theme). It returns `unchanged:true` when
already applied, is `mutates:false`, and does not change the Chart Grid's own
per-user chart theme.

`workspace.getActivity` lists bounded recent status/error history.

| Feedback send, product Tour, Practice Labs | **Human-only** | none |
| AI access grants, admin, data repair | **Human-only** | none |

Remaining limits inside covered areas:

- Crosshair sync between split panes is impossible (no chart-library setter);
  only symbol/interval linking exists.
- OHLC legend *collapse* and favorite drawing-tool *membership* have no public
  API (OHLC visibility and favorite order are scriptable).
- Heatmap historical periods are unsupported (current quotes only).
- Alert expiry is enforced only while the signed-in Alerts panel is mounted;
  alert `message`/`expiresAt` are rejected by production until the Alerts API
  update is deployed.
- UI-only: Heatmap error Retry, drawing-template library writes, saved-layout
  rename/delete, the Grid card enlarge dialog, file/clipboard exports and the
  secondary Multi/Indices/Peers grids' own sort/filter state.
  Discover ordinary controls through native inspection before attempting input.
  File/clipboard flows and protected controls still require the person; the
  presence of a generic click action is not permission to bypass those limits.

`workspace.setPanel` opens supported **bottom** panels; it does not select the
right Research sidebar. Use `research.show` for that. `workspace.getActivity`
contains bounded status/error history, not source or credentials.
Availability of a command in this repository or the source checkout is not
proof of its availability on another tab, browser, packaged release or cloud
deployment. Use `capabilities --tab` for the intended running tab and read
its domain readiness; read-only discovery cannot guarantee fresh candles.

The references retain their **isolated-source** generation provenance. On
October 29, 2026, read-only discovery briefly confirmed the then-advertised 211
descriptors on a ready production-origin tab in installed Desktop 0.1.6.
This did not execute domain mutations or certify native implementation parity.
Later discovery returned `ready:false` and no trusted tabs; no restart, reload
or origin switch was requested. Rediscover the intended ready tab before use.
Transport fixes in the local source are not installed merely by editing it.
The later descriptor, panel, feed-discovery and Scanner validation corrections,
and the workspace-UI commands that bring the source catalog to 241
descriptors (192 canonical, 49 aliases), are source/test verified only, not
certified by that earlier installed observation.

Never execute real broker orders, private diagnostic JavaScript, or arbitrary
host Python through these skills. Do not fetch, publish or sync user content
to another service unless explicitly requested and supported.

# tl-desktop command reference

Source-only snapshot from an isolated frontend registry; installed Desktop execution is not certified. Rediscover live availability before use.
Use explicit tab targeting and inspect the final JSON status. Do not guess IDs or grant permissions.

Do not infer grant permissions from `mutates`: Desktop discovery can omit structured grant metadata. Read [tl-desktop](../tl-desktop/SKILL.md) for the verified local-change versus cloud-watchlist access rules.

## `ui.waitIdle`

Wait until visually settled: chart history/replay/feed discovery done, no busy spinners or finite animations, fonts loaded, 2 stable frames. Returns {idle,waitedMs,pending}; TIMEOUT lists pending.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **none**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `timeoutMs` | Optional 100-60000, default 8000. |
| `scope` | Optional data-demo-id subtree. |

## `ui.listTargets`

List named demo targets {id,label,role,visible,rect{x,y,w,h} CSS px,viewport}; PII boxes have redact:true.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **none**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `scope` | Optional data-demo-id subtree. |

## `ui.getTargetRect`

Rect of one demo target, first visible unless nth. TARGET_NOT_FOUND/TARGET_HIDDEN.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **none**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Target id from ui.listTargets. |
| `nth` | Optional 0-based match index. |

## `demo.prepare`

Ephemeral presentation mode: hide tours/toasts/banners, optionally freeze clock labels, redact PII, hide cursor. Nothing persisted; no write grant. Returns previous; demo.reset restores.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **ui**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `hideTours` | bool, default true |
| `hideToasts` | bool, default true |
| `hideCookieBanner` | bool, default true |
| `freezeClock` | ISO time for clock labels |
| `redact` | bool |
| `cursor` | bool; false hides it |

## `demo.reset`

Leave presentation mode; clears redaction and frozen clock.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **ui**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

Parameters: `{}`.

## `demo.redact`

Blur PII (account, contact, broker ids, balances) plus optional selectors. Ephemeral.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **ui**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `enable` | Required bool |
| `selectors` | Optional up to 20 extra CSS selectors. |

## `workspace.getState`

Read this tab's account/permission state and screening source.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **none**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

Parameters: `{}`.

## `workspace.getActivity`

Read bounded command status/error-code history and active command count. Never returns credentials, source or command arguments.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **none**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

Parameters: `{}`.

## `workspace.setPanel`

Select a /charts bottom panel and expand/minimize it. Right-docked Backtesting toggles only its side panel unless dock is given. Returns expected placement; verify workspace.getState panels.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **panel**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `panel` | peers\|watchlists\|futures\|backtesting\|paper-trading\|intelligence\|indicators; simulation is a legacy alias |
| `expanded` | Optional boolean, default true. |
| `dock` | Optional bottom\|right, backtesting only: place it and select its tab. right fails DOCK_UNAVAILABLE under 720px. |

## `workspace.openSidebar`

Open/collapse a /charts right-sidebar section incl. More items. Layout only, no write grant. Confirm via workspace.getState sidebar.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **panel**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `panel` | watchlists\|indices\|heatmap\|scanner\|grid\|patterns\|alerts\|research\|dataWindow\|paperTrading\|contests |
| `expanded` | Optional boolean, default true |

## `workspace.setTheme`

Set this browser's app light/dark theme (same as Settings > Theme). Local UI preference only. Returns previous for restoring.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `theme` | light\|dark |

## Native Desktop controls

Run `tradinglead desktop ACTION --tab ACTUAL_TAB_ID` from the Desktop repository. App-level `getOrigin`, `setOrigin`, `logs`, `services` and `appInfo` take no `--tab`; `screenshot` takes an optional `--tab` (default: active tab); `setOrigin`, `logs` and `screenshot` take `--params JSON`.

- `status`: Read native readiness and reported permission state without requiring AI access.
- `activate`: Focus this explicit trusted tab without navigating or reloading it.
- `open-access`: Request the in-place permission panel. Only the user can enable grants; poll status for accessPanelOpen.
- `reconnect`: Request registration retry using existing grants. Disabled access opens the permission panel instead. Poll status.
- `getOrigin`: Read the app website origin, the cloud origin, whether it is local, and the trusted origins.
- `setOrigin`: Switch the website origin to "cloud"/https://tradinglead.in or a loopback dev server with an explicit port. params: { origin, path?, navigate? }. Navigates the active tab; poll tabs and desktop status.
- `screenshot`: Capture a PNG of the given tab (default: active trusted tab). params: { selector? } crops to the first matching element. Returns { path, bytes, width, height, tabId }; the file is private to the local user.
- `logs`: Read-only, redacted tail of Desktop diagnostics. params: { kind: "events"|"bars", tail?: 1-200 (default 50) }.
- `services`: Read feed registry, sidecar (no credentials), Python indicator runtime and updater status.
- `appInfo`: Read app version, Electron, build channel, dev mode, origin, agent protocol and per-tab catalog registration (entries, hash, rejected).

These controls cannot grant access. Discover them using `tradinglead desktop capabilities`.

# Demos and recordings

These commands make automated demo videos (Playwright + Remotion) and annotated
screenshot decks reliable. Exact fields are in [commands.md](commands.md).

| Command | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `ui.waitIdle {timeoutMs?, scope?}` | Waits until the app is visually settled: no chart widget, history or source loads, no feed discovery, no replay load, no visible busy spinners, no finite CSS or Web animations, fonts loaded, then two stable frames. Returns `{idle:true, waitedMs, pending:[]}`. If the app is still busy at the timeout it fails with `TIMEOUT`, and `data.pending` lists the blockers. The default timeout is 8 s and the range is 100 to 60000 ms. |
| `ui.listTargets {scope?}` | Lists named targets as `{id, nth, label, role, visible, rect:{x,y,w,h}, viewport:{w,h,dpr}}` in CSS px. Entries can also carry `redact:true` (PII to blur in post) and `frame:true` (resolved inside the TradingView chart frame). |
| `ui.getTargetRect {id, nth?}` | Returns one target, preferring visible matches. Fails with `TARGET_NOT_FOUND` (not mounted) or `TARGET_HIDDEN` (mounted but hidden or off-screen). |
| `demo.prepare {hideTours?, hideToasts?, hideCookieBanner?, freezeClock?, redact?, cursor?}` | Turns on presentation mode. Tours, toasts and banners are hidden by default. `freezeClock` takes an ISO date-time and replaces clock labels with that time. `cursor:false` hides the pointer. Sets `body[data-demo-mode]` and returns `{settings, previous}`. |
| `demo.reset` | Restores everything that `demo.prepare` and `demo.redact` changed. |
| `demo.redact {enable, selectors?}` | Blurs PII in the app: email, phone, account name, broker ids and balances (`[data-demo-redact]`), plus up to 20 extra CSS selectors. |

Policy: everything here is ephemeral CSS and attribute state. No preferences,
storage or tour-seen flags change, and reloading the page clears it.

- `ui.*` commands have effects `none`.
- `demo.*` commands are `mutates:false` with effect `ui`, so they need agent access but not the write grant. This follows the same precedent as layout-only commands such as `workspace.setTheme`.

## Recording recipe

1. Open the scene with normal commands, for example `chart.open` or `workspace.setPanel`.
2. Call `demo.prepare {"redact":true,"freezeClock":"2026-01-05T09:15:00+05:30"}`.
3. Before each shot, call `ui.waitIdle {"timeoutMs":15000}`.
4. Call `ui.getTargetRect {"id":"backtesting.run"}` to get click, zoom or callout boxes. For entries with `redact:true`, blur their rects in post too.
5. When finished, call `demo.reset`.

Rects use CSS px relative to the app viewport. Multiply by `viewport.dpr` to get
screenshot pixels. Re-read a rect after any layout change.

## Target ids

| Area | Ids |
| --- | --- |
| Chart | `chart.area`, `chart.toolbar`, `chart.feed`, `chart.layout`, `chart.interval`, `chart.symbolSearch`, `chart.indicators`, `chart.timezone` |
| Sidebars | `sidebar.left`, `sidebar.right`, `sidebar.panel`, `account.menu`, `watchlist.panel`, `alerts.panel`, `patterns.panel`, `grid.panel`, `paper.sidebar` |
| Screener | `screener.panel`, `screener.run`, `screener.results` |
| Bottom bar | `bottom.panel`, `bottom.tab.<tab>` |
| Backtesting | `backtesting.panel`, `backtesting.run`, `backtesting.summary`, `backtesting.views`, `backtesting.trades`, `backtesting.equity`, `backtesting.ledger` |
| Optimisation | `optimization.panel`, `optimization.run` |
| Paper trading | `paper.panel`, `paper.controls`, `paper.summary`, `paper.trades`, `paper.equity`, `paper.ledger` |
| Indicator Studio | `studio.panel`, `studio.editor`, `studio.run`, `studio.aiAccess` |
| Agent access | `agent.access` |

Notes on ids:

- Elements outside the chart frame that carry `data-demo-id` take precedence over frame targets with the same id.
- `chart.symbolSearch`, `chart.indicators` and `chart.timezone` always come from the TradingView frame. `chart.interval` may also come from it.
- Redaction-only entries use the id `redact.<kind>`, where kind is `initials`, `name`, `contact`, `account`, `brokerProfile` or `balance`. Their label is the kind, never the PII text.

## Browser use without Desktop (`window.__tlDemo`)

Playwright can call `await page.evaluate(() => window.__tlDemo.exec("ui.waitIdle", {}))`.
`window.__tlDemo.catalog()` lists the allowed commands.

The API exists only in these cases:

- a development build, or
- a page loaded as `?demo=<token>`, where the token matches `REACT_APP_DEMO_TOKEN` (at least 8 characters) and the host is loopback (`localhost`, `127.x`, `::1`).

It is never present on tradinglead.in or on LAN hosts.

It runs only:

- `ui.*` and `demo.*` commands,
- `chart.getState`, `workspace.getState` and `layout.getState`,
- `chart.open` and `workspace.setPanel`, but only outside production builds.

Every other command returns `FORBIDDEN`.

# Native UI input and local video recording

These are **native Desktop 0.1.9+ features**, not a frontend command namespace.
Desktop 0.1.8 and earlier do not contain them. Read
`tradinglead desktop capabilities` on the intended installation first. If the
actions below are absent, a new Desktop build is required; skills cannot add them.
No MCP, browser-debugging endpoint or arbitrary JavaScript execution is used.

## Connect and get human approval

Select the intended tab from `tradinglead tabs`, then:

```bash
tradinglead desktop ui-enable --tab TAB_ID --key enable-session-1
tradinglead desktop ui-status --tab TAB_ID
tradinglead desktop ui-inspect --tab TAB_ID
```

UI control requires an active, visible, ready `/charts` tab, local assistant
access, both existing write grants, and a **native dialog approved by a person**.
`ui-enable` cannot grant the underlying permissions. Approval expires after ten
minutes. Closing the visible AI control window revokes it. The person can also
use **Help > Stop AI control and recording** or **Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Escape**.
Switching tabs, changing accounts, navigating, pausing access or disabling a
grant invalidates UI consent. Request fresh consent; do not retarget another tab.

The current frontend marks chart surfaces, the normal Backtesting/Paper panel
and source editors as automation areas. `ui-inspect` reports `automationScope`
per control. **Desktop 0.1.10+** uses the existing
session approval for ordinary controls even when `automationScope` is false or
absent. Paper-trading quantity fields, portal dialogs and older unmarked chart
controls no longer need a separate confirmation for each click/type/key.
The native `ui-enable` capability description advertises this as "without
per-action prompts". The installed 0.1.9 release retains the old per-action
confirmation fallback until Desktop itself is updated; never dismiss or approve
those prompts programmatically, or force markers onto the page.
Login, purchases, credentials, broker setup, permission controls
and Guided Practice Labs remain human-operated. Visible credential dialogs,
unsupported frames and protected targets fail explicitly.

## Inspect and interact

`ui-inspect` lists at most 200 visible non-sensitive controls, including CSS
selectors, labels, roles, disabled/editable state and viewport rectangles.
It does not return input values. Optional `selector` scopes the search.
Optional `frames` is an ordered array of up to four same-origin iframe selectors.
It does not auto-scroll or silently choose between duplicate selector matches.

Every input command requires a fresh `--key`. Reuse the same key and identical
parameters only to reconcile the same operation. Retries are deduplicated by a
bounded in-memory cache, not a durable transaction log.

```bash
tradinglead desktop ui-click --tab TAB_ID --params '{"selector":"ACTUAL_CSS"}' --key click-1
tradinglead desktop ui-hover --tab TAB_ID --params '{"x":400,"y":250}' --key hover-1
tradinglead desktop ui-scroll --tab TAB_ID --params '{"selector":"ACTUAL_SCROLL_CONTAINER","deltaY":400}' --key scroll-1
tradinglead desktop ui-type --tab TAB_ID --params '{"selector":"ACTUAL_INPUT","text":"new text","replace":true}' --key type-1
tradinglead desktop ui-key --tab TAB_ID --params '{"selector":"ACTUAL_INPUT","key":"Enter"}' --key key-1
tradinglead desktop ui-disable --tab TAB_ID --key disable-session-1
```

Use **either** `selector` **or** `x,y` (CSS pixels relative to the top-level tab
viewport, not desktop/screenshot physical pixels). Native zoom is handled by the
app. For iframe contents, provide `frames`; coordinates can also resolve through
visible same-origin frames. Covered, hidden, disabled, ambiguous, transformed
frame or cross-origin targets are rejected rather than guessed.

- Click: `button:"left"|"right"` and `clickCount:1|2`; defaults left/single.
- Scroll: `deltaY` and optional `deltaX`, each -2000..2000; positive down/right.
- Type: nonempty Unicode `text`, maximum 16000 characters; `replace` defaults
  false. Use enabled text inputs, textareas or contenteditable editors.
- Key: `Enter`, `Escape`, `Tab`, `Backspace`, `Delete`, `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight`,
  `ArrowUp`, `ArrowDown`, `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`; optional `shift`.
  No system shortcuts, clipboard commands, file-picker input or arbitrary keys.
- `--params-file file.json` avoids shell quoting and command-line text exposure.

Input results say `dispatched:true, verified:false`. **Do not claim a saved
change from dispatch alone.** Inspect the UI, take an authorized screenshot or
read the domain state. Prefer domain commands for deterministic saves/backtests.

### Smooth interaction recipe

Run one operation at a time; the examples use placeholders from a fresh
`ui-inspect` result, not selectors to copy verbatim:

```bash
tradinglead desktop ui-inspect --tab TAB_ID --params '{"selector":"ACTUAL_PANEL"}'
tradinglead desktop ui-hover --tab TAB_ID --params '{"selector":"ACTUAL_CONTROL"}' --key reveal-1
tradinglead desktop ui-inspect --tab TAB_ID --params '{"selector":"ACTUAL_PANEL"}'
tradinglead desktop ui-click --tab TAB_ID --params '{"selector":"ACTUAL_CONTROL","button":"right"}' --key context-menu-1
tradinglead desktop ui-inspect --tab TAB_ID
```

Inspect the opened menu before selecting its actual item. Never assume a native
OS menu or protected dialog became automatable. For a lower item, scroll the
visible container by about 250-500 CSS pixels, inspect, then click the newly
visible target. Wheel events go to the target under the pointer; scrolling the
page does not necessarily scroll a nested panel. Do not click offscreen targets.

For editing, locate the actual editable input/textarea/contenteditable, use
`ui-type` with `replace:true`, then send Enter or click the real Apply button
only when that is the intended operation. The inspector omits values by design:
verify the resulting domain state rather than treating dispatch as a value read.
Choose `--params-file` for multiline source; empty strings, passwords and file
inputs are unsupported. For canvas targets, use a fresh authorized screenshot
and convert to **CSS viewport pixels**, or prefer a domain command.

With iframes, copy the ordered `frames` path from inspection and use it
consistently. Reinspect after zoom, resizing, scrolling, navigation or opening
an overlay. Do not press Escape blindly: it can discard an unsaved dialog.

### Recover without guessing

| Condition | Safe next step |
| --- | --- |
| Missing native action | Update Desktop; do not substitute `exec` or a debugging endpoint. |
| `UI_NOT_READY` | Confirm the intended visible `/charts` tab and current readiness; do not reload unsaved work. |
| `UI_WRITE_PERMISSION_REQUIRED` | The person must enable the existing grants. |
| `UI_APPROVAL_REQUIRED`, `UI_APPROVAL_DENIED`, `UI_CONTEXT_CHANGED` | Stop; obtain fresh human approval when appropriate. Do not retry approval with new keys in a loop. |
| Hidden, covered or ambiguous target | Inspect again, close only a known safe overlay, or scroll the correct container; never pick a random match. |
| Human-only target or unsupported frame | Ask the person to operate it; no marker injection or protection bypass. |
| Dispatched input but unchanged UI | Inspect the actual outcome and readiness. Reconcile an uncertain operation with the same key; do not duplicate a potentially saved write. |

## Record only the selected tab

```bash
tradinglead desktop record-start --tab TAB_ID --params '{"durationMs":30000,"fps":5}' --key record-1
tradinglead desktop record-status --tab TAB_ID --params '{"recordingId":"RETURNED_ID"}'
tradinglead desktop record-stop --tab TAB_ID --params '{"recordingId":"RETURNED_ID"}' --key stop-record-1
```

Start requests **separate human consent**; UI-input permission is not required.
The tab must remain active, visible, trusted, ready and locally accessible.
A compact, draggable recording window shows elapsed/limit timers, a duration
progress bar and a **Stop & save** button. It switches to **Saving...** while
finalizing, with the button disabled to prevent repeat clicks.
Closing that window also stops and finalizes. Automatic limits:

- Duration: 1000..600000ms; default 60000ms. FPS: 1..10; default 5.
- Video-only VP8 WebM; no microphone, system audio or whole-desktop capture.
- At most 1920x1080, aspect ratio preserved; one recording at a time.
- Maximum 64MiB per clip and 20 recording attempts per app process.

Poll until `state:"completed"` and use the returned local `path`. Files are
private, stored under `~/.tradinglead-desktop/recordings`, and never uploaded.
`stopping` is not completion. A failed job returns `state:"failed"` with a code
and no completed path. Capture/encoder/disk failures discard that clip's partial
file rather than presenting it as a completed video. Quit/crash during capture
can lose the current clip; stop and wait for completion before quitting.

Tab/context changes stop capture and finalize already accepted frames with
`stoppedReason`; they never continue recording another tab. Visible chart/account
information can appear in an approved clip: arrange/redact the UI beforehand.
Cross-origin frames and visible credential/consent dialogs are not supported.
files.tl-charts/SKILL.md:
---
name: tl-charts
description: Control the TradingLead chart workspace through discovered commands. Use for chart symbol/feed/interval navigation, history navigation and go-to-date, snapshots, reload/live, native manual replay, chart type/scale/range/timezone/OHLC legend, Compare/Overlay symbols, toolbar actions and screenshots, native studies and indicator templates, user drawings and drawing templates, split-chart layouts with pane targeting and symbol/interval linking, saved chart layouts and the Chart Grid. Watchlists/market panels belong to tl-markets, saved alerts to tl-alerts, weekday/time-window studies to tl-patterns and multi-stock scans to tl-screening.
---

# TradingLead charts, drawings, layouts and Chart Grid

Start with [tl-desktop](../tl-desktop/SKILL.md). Exact fields:
[commands.md](commands.md). Detailed references:

- [workflows.md](workflows.md): context, permissions, snapshots, studies,
  drawing templates, native replay and manual-only boundaries.
- [drawings.md](drawings.md): `drawings.*` list/create/update/toolbar modes.
- [layouts-grid.md](layouts-grid.md): split layouts, active-pane targeting,
  saved chart layouts and the Chart Grid (`layout.*`, `grid.*`).

Discover the intended tab's installed catalog; source support does not establish
packaged or cloud availability. Watchlists, symbol details, peers, indices,
heatmap, Market Intelligence, Futures, universes and raw candles belong to
[tl-markets](../tl-markets/SKILL.md). Saved price alerts belong to
[tl-alerts](../tl-alerts/SKILL.md). The **Patterns** sidebar belongs to
[tl-patterns](../tl-patterns/SKILL.md).

## Every chart command targets the active pane

`chart.*`, `studies.*`, `studyTemplates.*`, `drawingTemplates.*`, `drawings.*` and indicator
commands operate on the **active split-chart pane** only; none accepts a
`paneId`. In a split layout, read `layout.getState`, select a pane with
`layout.set {"activePane":"chart-2"}`, and confirm the new active pane is
ready before sending chart commands. See [layouts-grid.md](layouts-grid.md).
Do not change pane, account or chart context while an operation is pending.

## Discover, navigate, verify

1. Read `chart.getState` and `feeds.list`. Chart feeds and the SQL-backed
   screener are different data sources. A feed listed in the catalog is not
   necessarily connected or available for a given ticker/resolution; use
   current status rather than an assumed fallback. Website provider IDs (for
   example `web-fyers`, `web-dhan`, `web-binance`, `web-alpaca`) are distinct
   from Desktop-local IDs such as `fyers` or `kite`. Use `feeds.list` for the
   addressed tab, not these examples.
2. To change context, use `chart.open` with an explicit canonical symbol,
   discovered feed and supported interval (interval changes also use
   `chart.open`; `chart.setView` has no interval field):

```json
{"type":"chart.open","params":{"symbol":"NSE:TCS-EQ","feed":"default","interval":"1D"}}
```

3. An acknowledgement such as `navigationRequested:true,dataReady:false` is not
   loaded data. Poll `chart.getState` until the intended context matches and
   `data.dataReady` is `true` (or an explicit error occurs). `data.ready` only
   means the chart widget is ready and turns true before candles arrive;
   `dataReady` additionally requires `history.state:"ready"`, settled feed
   discovery/source switching and no replay load. Do not switch provider to hide
   a failure. `history.state === "exhausted"` means the loader found no earlier
   history in that window, not a certified provider boundary.
4. Read `chart.snapshot` with `bars` from 1 to 25. Check actual timestamps,
   schema, missing values and truncation. This is a bounded native chart export,
   not an arbitrary historical-data download. For raw candles without the chart,
   use `marketData.getBars` in [tl-markets](../tl-markets/SKILL.md).

`chart.reload` uses the current provider and can consume provider quota.
`chart.setLive` requests a boolean live-update state; confirm the actual stream
in `chart.getState`. Receipt time, socket connection and an updating UI are not
proof of market freshness. `mutates:false` does not mean side-effect-free:
navigation, reload, live controls and panel selection can change visible state
or use quota. These controls need external AI access but no retry key. Study
writes use the **indicator** grant; every other `mutates:true` chart command
(view, compare, actions, drawings, layouts, grid, replay, template apply) uses
the **general local write** grant, a signed-in account and a retry key.

## History navigation and native replay

Discover `chart.navigateHistory` in the addressed tab before using it:

```json
{"type":"chart.navigateHistory","params":{"action":"date","date":"2023-06-12"}}
```

```json
{"type":"chart.navigateHistory","params":{"action":"latest"}}
```

```json
{"type":"chart.navigateHistory","params":{"action":"previous"}}
```

```json
{"type":"chart.navigateHistory","params":{"action":"retry"}}
```

Dates must be real UTC `YYYY-MM-DD` dates no later than today in UTC; omit `date` for the
other actions. These controls can fetch provider history. An accepted request
does not prove completion: inspect `chart.getState.navigation`, including
`loading`, `error`, `message`, `anchor` (Unix seconds), `historical`,
`previous` (availability), `checkedThrough` (the searched horizon in Unix
seconds, not proof that every candle exists), and `nextAvailable` (a discovered
candle, not a guaranteed coverage boundary).

Ordinary historical stock/timeframe changes retain the last valid cursor time
and horizontal position, or the chart centre when there is no cursor anchor.
The new interval loads a bounded window, not every finer candle across the old
range. Loading uses the actual viewport width and candle spacing and checks
the visible right side after positioning, without requiring another scroll.
Moving further right loads additional bounded historical windows; live ticks
are not used to fill missing history. Latest prices fetches recent history at
a readable zoom without enabling live updates, and Previous view restores the
saved context and spacing. Returning to a saved recent view releases historical
live suppression without changing the saved live-update preference. Weekly and
monthly navigation selects the containing calendar candle, keeping the researched
day for a subsequent return to an intraday interval. Neither action implicitly ends manual
or paper replay.

The chart-local date form navigates only on **Go** or Enter, not while editing;
the same date can be submitted again. The field and heading label UTC explicitly.
Previous view and Choose date remain available during loading. Historical page
loading has a 30-second recovery watchdog; a timeout is a retryable failure, not
proof that candles do not exist. Fullscreen transfers retain input focus and drafts.

Missing target history identifies the requested context and offers recovery.
The chart can check other supported intervals at that date and offer verified
choices in `navigation.alternatives`. These are explicit interval changes,
not automatic substitution or a repair of the missing interval's stored data.
An empty forward search only means no later candles in the checked window;
it does not certify the end of the provider's history. Never switch feeds,
invent candles, or equate latest *available* prices with fresh market data.
Navigation state is per-chart, in memory, not a saved cross-device preference.


`chart.replayControl` requests native manual Replay `select`, `play`, `pause`,
`step`, `speed` (0.1-200 bars/second) or `end`. Selection opens the native
picker; a person still chooses a candle. Paper replay uses
[tl-paper-trading](../tl-paper-trading/SKILL.md). Full recipes and caveats are
in [workflows.md](workflows.md).

## View, scale, range and timezone

`chart.viewState` (read, no key) returns chart type, interval, symbol, main
price-scale mode (native codes `0` normal, `1` log, `2` percent, `3` indexed)
and auto-scale, visible range, current timezone, up to 100 available timezone
IDs, the drawing-toolbar state (selected tool, magnet, lock-all, hide-all),
`legend` (`ohlcVisible`, `collapseSupported:false`) and `favorites` (the
mounted favorite drawing tools in order, `membershipEditable:false`).

`chart.setView` changes one or more of:

- `chartType`: `bars`, `candles`, `line`, `area`, `line-break`, `heikin-ashi`,
  `hollow-candles`, `baseline`, `high-low`, `columns`, `line-with-markers`,
  `stepline`, `hlc-area`.
- `priceScale`: `{mode?: normal|log|percent, autoScale?: boolean}`.
- `visibleRange`: `{preset: 5y|1y|6m|3m|1m|5d|1d}` (keeps the current
  resolution) **or** `{from, to}` epoch seconds. Not with `goToDate`.
- `goToDate`: a completed UTC date `YYYY-MM-DD`, a whole-second ISO timestamp
  with an explicit offset (`2026-03-12T09:30:00+05:30` or `...Z`), or epoch
  seconds. Routed through the guarded history navigator; future times are
  rejected.
- `timezone`: an exact ID from `chart.viewState.timezones`; the result
  verifies the native timezone matches (`CHART_UPDATE_UNCONFIRMED` if not).
- `legend`: `{ohlcVisible: boolean}` shows/hides the OHLC values in the legend
  and is verified by re-reading the saved state. Refused
  (`CHART_API_UNAVAILABLE`) inside a native multi-chart widget. Legend
  *collapse* has no public API and stays UI-only.

```json
{"type":"chart.setView","params":{"chartType":"heikin-ashi","priceScale":{"mode":"log"},"visibleRange":{"preset":"6m"}},"idempotencyKey":"chart-view-001"}
```

Range and date changes are refused during native/paper replay (`REPLAY_ACTIVE`)
and never end replay for you. The result is `requested:true,
historyConfirmed:false` plus a fresh view read: a range request may fetch
history through the selected feed, but does not prove candles exist, data is
fresh or the final visible bounds were achieved. Reread `chart.getState`,
`chart.viewState` and `chart.snapshot` after it settles.

## Compare and Overlay symbols

`chart.compare` handles only native **Compare/Overlay** studies (the top bar
**A+B** button), never other studies. It is `mutates:true` for every action,
so even `list` needs the write grant and a retry key.

- `{"action":"list","offset":0,"limit":50}` returns ID, kind and symbol.
- `{"action":"add","symbol":"NSE:INFY-EQ","kind":"compare"}`; `kind` is
  `compare` (default) or `overlay` (forced onto the main pane). Adds use the
  chart's selected feed with no fallback and cap at 20 comparisons.
- `{"action":"remove","id":"EXACT_LISTED_ID"}` removes only that comparison.

```json
{"type":"chart.compare","params":{"action":"add","symbol":"NSE:INFY-EQ"},"idempotencyKey":"compare-add-001"}
```

Add/remove are refused during replay. A created comparison returns
`calculationConfirmed:false`: inspect the chart before claiming the compared
series loaded.

## Toolbar actions and screenshots

`chart.action` requests one native action: `undo`, `redo`, `settings`
(opens chart properties), `screenshot`, `fullscreen` (requires
`enabled:true|false`), `resetScale` (main-series auto-scale), `objectTree`,
`compareDialog` or `goToDate` (opens the native dialogs). Undo/redo and the
compare/date dialogs are refused during replay. Most actions return
`requested:true,confirmed:false`: dialogs need a person to finish them and the
browser may deny fullscreen.

```json
{"type":"chart.action","params":{"action":"screenshot"},"idempotencyKey":"chart-shot-001"}
```

`screenshot` returns `{image,width,height}`: a PNG data URL thumbnail of at most
640x360 and 256 KiB. It is not saved, downloaded or an OS screenshot, and it does
not prove data freshness. Do not repeat it in loops; the payload is large.

## Native studies and drawing templates

1. Page `studies.list`, read `studies.inputs` for an exact name, then
   `studies.apply` with declared inputs, a retry key and the indicator grant.
2. `studies.applied` lists unmanaged native studies; `studies.setVisibility` and
   `studies.remove` need the exact `entityId`, `name` and current
   `expectedVisible`. They do not target managed Pine/Python/backtest studies,
   drawings or Compare series.
3. `drawingTemplates.state/list/apply` restyle one user-selected editable
   drawing. Template save/rename/delete remain UI-only.
4. `studyTemplates.manage` handles **native indicator templates** (the top-bar
   templates menu), not drawing styles or chart layouts. It is
   `permission:"indicators"` and `mutates:true` for every action, so even
   `list` needs the indicator grant and a retry key. It needs a signed-in
   chart with native template storage (`STUDY_TEMPLATES_UNAVAILABLE`).
   - `{"action":"list","offset":0,"limit":50}` → `{items:[{name}],total,truncated}`.
   - `{"action":"save","name":"Momentum set"}` saves the current native
     studies without symbol/interval; an existing name fails
     `STUDY_TEMPLATE_EXISTS` unless `replace:true`.
   - `{"action":"apply","name":"...","confirm":true}` **replaces** the chart's
     native studies. Symbol, interval and currency stored in the template are
     stripped (only `chart.open` changes context). Refused during replay and
     whenever managed TLScript/Python/backtest studies are on the chart or in
     the template (`MANAGED_STUDIES_PRESENT`); remove them through their own
     lifecycle first. Returns `requested:true, calculationConfirmed:false`;
     verify with `studies.applied`.
   - `{"action":"delete","name":"...","confirm":true}`; unknown names fail
     `STUDY_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND`.

```json
{"type":"studyTemplates.manage","params":{"action":"apply","name":"Momentum set","confirm":true},"idempotencyKey":"study-template-apply-001"}
```

Built-in TradingView studies are not Pine source programs; custom TLScript and
Python indicators belong to [tl-tlscript](../tl-tlscript/SKILL.md) and
[tl-python](../tl-python/SKILL.md). Recipes: [workflows.md](workflows.md).

## Drawings, layouts and Chart Grid (summary)

- `drawings.list/create/update/setMode`: page, create allowlisted fixed-point
  drawings, hide/lock/remove exact user drawings, choose a toolbar tool or
  magnet/lock-all/hide-all, reorder favorite drawing tools, and the confirmed
  `removeAll`. Managed visuals and studies are never touched. See
  [drawings.md](drawings.md).
- `layout.getState/set/saved`: split layout, active pane, maximize, split
  sizes, fullscreen, symbol/interval pane linking and saved chart layouts for
  the active pane.
- `grid.open/getState/configure`: open the right-sidebar Chart Grid with
  explicit symbols or a completed Scanner run (all, filtered or selected rows),
  then read and configure it, including theme, width, expand, copied chart
  indicators, opening a card on the chart and close/open-page.
  See [layouts-grid.md](layouts-grid.md).

## Boundaries

- Existing studies, drawings, comparisons and chart context belong to the
  user. Do not remove or replace them as a shortcut.
- Broker setup, credentials and data-source settings are separate human UI
  flows. `feeds.list` discovers availability; it does not configure brokers.
- No native symbol-search command: use `chart.open` with an explicit symbol.
- Chart/style property editing beyond `chart.setView` stays interactive after
  `chart.action {"action":"settings"}`; there is no raw property override.
- UI-only, no public API: OHLC legend collapse, adding/removing favorite
  drawing tools (order is scriptable), crosshair sync between split panes,
  saved-layout rename/delete and drawing styles beyond templates.
- A report about a saved backtest must use that run's frozen evidence, not
  whatever candles happen to be on the current chart.

# tl-charts command reference

Source-only snapshot from an isolated frontend registry; installed Desktop execution is not certified. Rediscover live availability before use.
Use explicit tab targeting and inspect the final JSON status. Do not guess IDs or grant permissions.

Do not infer grant permissions from `mutates`: Desktop discovery can omit structured grant metadata. Read [tl-desktop](../tl-desktop/SKILL.md) for the verified local-change versus cloud-watchlist access rules.

## `chart.viewState`

Read bounded native chart view/scale/timezone and drawing toolbar state.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **none**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

Parameters: `{}`.

## `chart.setView`

Set native view; ranges request positioning, not verified history. Symbol/interval: chart.open. Date: guarded navigator.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **navigate, quota, network, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `chartType` | Optional named chart type. |
| `priceScale` | {mode?:normal\|percent\|log,autoScale?:boolean} |
| `visibleRange` | {preset:5y\|1y\|6m\|3m\|1m\|5d\|1d} OR {from,to} epoch seconds |
| `goToDate` | UTC date, offset ISO timestamp, or epoch seconds. |
| `timezone` | Available timezone ID from viewState. |
| `legend` | {ohlcVisible:boolean} |

## `chart.compare`

List/add/remove native Compare/Overlay only; never other studies. Adds use selected feed; no fallback.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **navigate, quota, network, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `action` | list\|add\|remove |
| `symbol` | Required for add. |
| `kind` | Optional add: compare (default)\|overlay. |
| `id` | Exact listed id for remove. |
| `offset` | Optional list offset. |
| `limit` | Optional list 1-50. |

## `chart.action`

Request native toolbar action. Screenshot returns bounded PNG, not a file. Replay guards undo/redo/date/compare.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **panel, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `action` | undo\|redo\|settings\|screenshot\|fullscreen\|resetScale\|objectTree\|compareDialog\|goToDate |
| `enabled` | Required boolean only for fullscreen. |

## `drawings.list`

Page user drawings only: id/tool, up to 10 time/price points, visible/locked; excludes managed visuals.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **none**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `offset` | Optional 0-10000. |
| `limit` | Optional 1-50, default 50. |

## `drawings.create`

Create one allowlisted user drawing with exact tool point count. Epoch seconds/prices; no raw overrides.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `tool` | Allowlisted tool; see public guide. |
| `points` | 1-7 {time:integer epoch seconds,price:finite} |
| `text` | Optional text for text tool, max 500. |
| `locked` | Optional boolean. |

## `drawings.update`

Hide/lock/remove up to 50 exact user drawing IDs; never studies or managed visuals. Preflights all targets; not transactional.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `ids` | 1-50 unique IDs from list. |
| `visible` | Optional boolean. |
| `locked` | Optional boolean. |
| `remove` | Optional true; exclusive with visible/locked. |

## `drawings.setMode`

Set drawing modes/tool or reorder existing favorites. Confirmed removeAll deletes all user drawings, preserving managed visuals.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `tool` | Optional allowlisted drawing/cursor/brush/measure/zoom tool. |
| `magnet` | Optional boolean. |
| `lockAll` | Optional boolean. |
| `hideAll` | Optional boolean. |
| `favoriteOrder` | All current favorite tool IDs from chart.viewState, ordered; max 50. |
| `removeAll` | Optional true. |
| `confirm` | Required true only with removeAll. |

## `studyTemplates.manage`

Native indicator templates, not drawing styles/layouts. Apply replaces native studies only, preserving symbol/interval; no replay. Indicator grant/retry key required, including list.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.
Local indicator/backtesting grant required.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `action` | list\|save\|apply\|delete |
| `name` | Required except list; max 80. |
| `replace` | save only: true to overwrite. |
| `confirm` | Required true for apply/delete. |
| `offset` | list only, 0-10000. |
| `limit` | list only, 1-50. |

## `layout.getState`

Read split-chart layout: active pane, maximized pane, split sizes and each pane's last symbol/feed/interval. chart.*/studies.*/indicators.* always target the active pane.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **none**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `saved` | Optional boolean: also list up to 50 saved chart layouts (needs sign-in). |

## `layout.set`

Change split layout, active pane (retargets chart.* commands), focus/restore, split sizes, fullscreen or pane linking.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **navigate, panel, quota, network, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `layout` | single\|columns\|rows\|grid |
| `activePane` | Pane id in layout |
| `maximize` | bool |
| `horizontal` | 25-75 |
| `vertical` | 25-75 |
| `fullscreen` | bool |
| `sync` | {symbol?,interval?} bools: active pane drives others |

## `layout.saved`

Save the active pane's chart as a named saved layout, or load a saved layout id (from layout.getState saved:true) into the active pane, replacing its chart.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **navigate, panel, quota, network, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `action` | save\|load. |
| `name` | save: 1-64 chars. |
| `id` | load: saved layout id. |

## `grid.getState`

Read the mounted Chart Grid: settings, universe, ranking, paging and a bounded page of card symbols with load status.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **none**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `offset` | Optional 0-499 card offset. |
| `limit` | Optional 1-100, default 24. |
| `options` | Optional boolean: include universe choices (max 200). |

## `grid.configure`

Change the mounted Chart Grid; source/sort/filter/paging changes reset page. Verify with grid.getState.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **panel, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `universe` | getState option |
| `timeframe` | 5-1M |
| `candles` | 50-500 |
| `density` | size |
| `pageSize` | 6\|12\|18\|24 |
| `paging` | pages\|more |
| `indicators` | sma20\|ema50 |
| `volume` | bool |
| `sort` | {field,direction} |
| `filters` | partial; null clears |
| `page` | 1-based |
| `linkTimeframe` | bool |
| `refresh` | true |
| `chartIndicators` | copy\|basic |
| `theme` | id |
| `width` | px |
| `expanded` | bool |
| `openCard` | page symbol to active chart |
| `panel` | close\|openPage, alone |

## `grid.open`

Open the Chart Grid sidebar, optionally with explicit symbols or a completed visible scan's tickers in grid order.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **navigate, quota, network, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `symbols` | 1-500 tickers |
| `runId` | Screening runId |
| `scope` | all\|filtered\|selected scan rows |
| `label` | 1-120 chars |
| `timeframe` | Optional |
| `candles` | Optional |
| `pageSize` | Optional |

## `chart.getState`

Read active chart context and history/live/navigation status. ready=widget only; poll dataReady (verified candles) before reading data. feedCatalog reports broker-catalog issues separately from error. Receipt time is not market freshness.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **none**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

Parameters: `{}`.

## `chart.snapshot`

Export chart bars/study values without fetching. Check timestamps, completeness and truncation.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **none**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `bars` | Optional 1-25 trailing rows, default 5. |

## `chart.setLive`

Toggle supported live updates; may use broker quota. Requires AI access. Verify chart.getState.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **quota, network**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

Request history reload; may use provider quota. Verify readiness with chart.getState.

Browse bounded history. Never ends replay or enables live. Verify chart.getState.navigation.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.

Apply an exact saved template to the currently selected user drawing. Requires sign-in, local write approval and retry key; never creates or deletes drawings.

Discover chart feeds. Inspect discovery.status: failed broker discovery returns only default with an explicit error and bounded discovery.reason, never cached brokers. Chart feeds do not change the backend screening source.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.

Navigate this tab to an explicit symbol, chart feed and interval. This is not a broker trade.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
