# Drawings on the active chart

Part of [tl-charts](SKILL.md); exact fields in [commands.md](commands.md).
These commands cover the left drawing toolbar and user drawings on the
**active pane** only (select it first with `layout.set`; see
[layouts-grid.md](layouts-grid.md)). Every `drawings.*` write is `mutates:true`:
sign-in, the general local write grant and a retry key. Commands are refused
while the chart context changes; reread after any uncertain write.

## What counts as a user drawing

`drawings.list` and `drawings.update` see only user-editable drawings. They
exclude indicator/study shapes and managed chart visuals: shapes owned by a
study, not user-editable, hidden from the object tree or not saved with the
chart. They are never a way to remove
studies; use `studies.*` for native studies.

## List

```json
{"type":"drawings.list","params":{"offset":0,"limit":50}}
```

`offset` 0-10000, `limit` 1-50 (default 50). Items are
`{id, tool, points, pointsTruncated, visible, locked}` with at most 10
`{time, price}` points each, plus `total` and `truncated`. Page until
`truncated` is false before claiming a complete inventory.

## Create

`drawings.create` builds one drawing with the exact point count for its tool:

| Points | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | `horizontal_line`, `vertical_line`, `horizontal_ray`, `text` |
| 2 | `trend_line`, `ray`, `extended`, `arrow`, `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `fib_retracement`, `date_range`, `price_range`, `date_and_price_range` |
| 3 | `parallel_channel`, `triangle` |
| 4 | `abcd_pattern` |
| 5 | `xabcd_pattern` |
| 7 | `head_and_shoulders` |

Each point is `{time, price}`: `time` is integer epoch **seconds** (0 to
8640000000000), `price` is finite with absolute value at most 1e15. `text`
(single line, at most 500 characters) is allowed only for the `text` tool;
`locked` is an optional boolean. There are no raw style overrides; restyle an
existing selected drawing with `drawingTemplates.apply`.

```json
{"type":"drawings.create","params":{"tool":"trend_line","points":[{"time":1717200000,"price":3800},{"time":1719792000,"price":3950}]},"idempotencyKey":"draw-trend-001"}
```

The result is the created drawing's projection. `DRAWING_CREATE_FAILED` means
the chart did not confirm a drawing; list before retrying with the same key.
Choose times inside loaded history when the drawing must be visible.

## Hide, lock or remove exact drawings

```json
{"type":"drawings.update","params":{"ids":["EXACT_ID_FROM_LIST"],"locked":true},"idempotencyKey":"draw-lock-001"}
```

`ids` is 1-50 unique IDs from `drawings.list`. Send `visible` and/or `locked`,
**or** `remove:true` alone. All targets are preflighted (`DRAWING_NOT_FOUND`
aborts before any change), but the batch is not transactional: if a later item
fails, earlier items may already be changed. `CHART_UPDATE_UNCONFIRMED` means the
final state did not match; list again before retrying. Remove only drawings the
user asked to remove.

## Toolbar modes and remove-all

`drawings.setMode` mirrors the left drawing toolbar:

- `tool`: any create tool above, or `cursor`, `dot`, `arrow_cursor`, `eraser`,
  `measure`, `zoom`, `brush`, `highlighter`, `polyline`, `path`.
- `magnet`, `lockAll`, `hideAll`: booleans.

```json
{"type":"drawings.setMode","params":{"tool":"cursor","magnet":false},"idempotencyKey":"draw-mode-001"}
```

The result reports the observed `magnet`/`lockAll`/`hideAll` values
(`CHART_UPDATE_UNCONFIRMED` if they differ) and, for a tool, `requestedTool`
with `confirmed` (whether the toolbar now shows it). Selecting a tool only arms interactive drawing; it does not
create a drawing (use `drawings.create`). `hideAll`/`lockAll` are view toggles
and do not edit individual drawings.

Remove-all is a separate, exact request: `{"removeAll":true,"confirm":true}` and
no other fields. It deletes every user drawing (no count cap; it yields every 50
removals and stops if the chart context changes), never studies or managed
visuals, and returns `{removed (first 50 IDs), removedCount, truncated}`. If any
user drawing remains it fails `CHART_UPDATE_UNCONFIRMED`; list before retrying.
Use it only when the user explicitly asked to clear all drawings; list first and
report the count.

## Favorite drawing tools order

`chart.viewState.favorites` returns `{available, tools, truncated,
membershipEditable:false}` for the favorite drawings toolbar. Reorder it with an
exclusive request listing **every** current favorite exactly once (max 50):

```json
{"type":"drawings.setMode","params":{"favoriteOrder":["LineToolTrendLine","LineToolHorzLine"]},"idempotencyKey":"draw-fav-order-001"}
```

Use the exact IDs from `chart.viewState`; adding or removing favorites fails
`INVALID_PARAMS`. `FAVORITES_UNAVAILABLE` means the toolbar is not shown or a
drag is in progress; `FAVORITES_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` means nothing changed. The
order is stored locally in this app, not synced. Changing which tools are
favorites has no public API and stays UI-only.

## Read toolbar state

`chart.viewState.drawingMode` returns the selected tool and the magnet,
lock-all and hide-all states without a retry key.

## UI-only

Drawing style/property editing (beyond templates), drawing-template library
save/rename/delete, freehand stroke content, favorite-tool membership and
object-tree reordering remain interactive.

# Split layouts, saved chart layouts and Chart Grid

Part of [tl-charts](SKILL.md); exact fields in [commands.md](commands.md).
Writes (`layout.set`, `layout.saved`, `grid.open`, `grid.configure`) are
`mutates:true`: sign-in, general local write grant and a retry key. Reads need
only AI access. All require `/charts` mounted in the addressed tab for the
current account (`LAYOUT_UNAVAILABLE` / `GRID_UNAVAILABLE` otherwise).

## Split-chart layout and the active pane

```json
{"type":"layout.getState","params":{}}
```

Returns the layout (`single`, `columns`, `rows`, `grid`), active pane
(`main-chart`, `chart-2`, `chart-3`, `chart-4`), maximized pane, split sizes and
each pane's **last snapshot** of symbol/feed/interval, plus `sync`
(`{symbol,interval}`) and, when present, `syncSkipped`. Use `chart.getState` for
live readiness.

**Every `chart.*`, `studies.*`, `studyTemplates.*`, `indicators.*`,
`drawingTemplates.*` and `drawings.*` command targets only the active pane.** To work on another pane:

```json
{"type":"layout.set","params":{"layout":"columns","activePane":"chart-2"},"idempotencyKey":"layout-pane2-001"}
```

Then read `layout.getState` and wait for `activeReady:true` before chart
commands. `layout.set` accepts `layout`, `activePane` (must exist in the
resulting layout), `maximize`, `horizontal`/`vertical` split percentages (25-75)
`fullscreen` and `sync`; at least one field is required and validation happens
before anything changes. Switching to `single` keeps panes 2-4 mounted but hidden.
The top bar **A+B** button is Compare (`chart.compare`), not a pane feature.

### Linking panes (symbol / interval)

`sync: {symbol?, interval?}` toggles the layout menu's **Link symbol** /
**Link interval** switches (saved with the split-layout preferences). While
linked, the **active pane drives the others**: its symbol/interval changes are
pushed to the other visible panes, and turning a link on aligns them
immediately.

```json
{"type":"layout.set","params":{"layout":"grid","sync":{"symbol":true,"interval":true}},"idempotencyKey":"layout-link-001"}
```

- Symbols follow only into panes on the **same feed** (feeds use different
  symbol namespaces); interval links ignore feeds.
- Panes that are not mounted, or are skipped because of a different feed, are
  listed in `layout.getState.syncSkipped`.
- Linking is one-way from the active pane. A pane that appears because the
  layout grew is aligned only on the next active-pane change or when a link is
  re-enabled; send `sync` again after changing `layout` if alignment matters.
- Propagation is asynchronous (each pane applies once ready). Verify by reading
  `layout.getState.panes` (and `chart.getState` after activating a pane).
- Linking has no effect in `single` layout. There is **no crosshair sync**
  between panes: it is not possible with the chart library API. Without links,
  open each pane's context with `chart.open` after activating it.

## Saved chart layouts

```json
{"type":"layout.getState","params":{"saved":true}}
```

`saved:true` (sign-in required) adds up to 50 saved layouts with `id`, `name`,
`symbol`, `interval`, plus `current`, `total` and `truncated`.

```json
{"type":"layout.saved","params":{"action":"save","name":"Swing setup"},"idempotencyKey":"layout-save-001"}
```

```json
{"type":"layout.saved","params":{"action":"load","id":"EXACT_SAVED_ID"},"idempotencyKey":"layout-load-001"}
```

`save` (`name` 1-64 characters) saves the active pane's chart. `load` replaces
the active pane's chart with a listed layout and returns `loadRequested:true`;
verify with `chart.getState`. Both fail with `CHART_CHANGED` if the active pane
changes mid-request; a `LAYOUT_TIMEOUT` is not rollback, so check before
retrying. Loading discards the pane's unsaved chart state: confirm with the user
first. Saved-layout rename/delete are UI-only.

## Chart Grid

The Grid (right sidebar **Grid**) is a cloud-backed card gallery, separate
from split layouts and Historical Patterns. Cards use cloud history only, with
no broker fallback; ranking uses stored summary candles, so rank values and card
values can differ.

### Open

```json
{"type":"grid.open","params":{"runId":"COMPLETED_SCREENING_RUN_ID","label":"Breakouts","timeframe":"1D"},"idempotencyKey":"grid-open-001"}
```

- `{}` opens the Grid with its current universe.
- `symbols`: 1-500 exchange-qualified tickers (for example `NSE:INFY-EQ`).
- `runId`: a completed, visible Scanner run; tickers in result-grid order,
  deduplicated, up to about 1025 rows, with `scanRows` and `truncated`.
- `scope` (only with `runId`): `all` (default, every result row), `filtered`
  (rows that survive the Scanner results grid's current filters) or `selected`
  (selected rows that survive the filters). `filtered`/`selected` read the
  results grid through read-only `screening.getAnalysis`; they fail
  `ANALYSIS_CHANGED` if the grid changes mid-read (retry) and `NO_SYMBOLS` if
  nothing qualifies. `truncated` is also true when some rows lack a ticker.
- `label`, `timeframe`, `candles`, `pageSize` apply only with `symbols`/`runId`.

It waits up to 8 seconds for the Grid to mount and returns
`verify:"grid.getState"`; acceptance is not loaded cards.

### Read

```json
{"type":"grid.getState","params":{"offset":0,"limit":24,"options":true}}
```

Returns `active`, `expanded`, settings, `theme`, `sidebar` (width/min/max/narrow),
`linkTimeframe`, `chartIndicators` (`{count,symbol}` when copied, else null),
universe (label, total, loading/error, handoff),
`arrange` (shown, filtered out, unranked, `rankingNeeded`, `rankPending`,
ranking error/time), paging, loading/history errors, a page of cards
(`symbol`, `status`, optional `rank`/`error`) and, with `options:true`, up to
200 universe choices. `offset` 0-499, `limit` 1-100 (default 24).

### Configure

```json
{"type":"grid.configure","params":{"timeframe":"1D","sort":{"field":"volumeRatio","direction":"desc"},"filters":{"changeMin":2}},"idempotencyKey":"grid-config-001"}
```

- `universe`: a `value` from `grid.getState {"options":true}` (or `handoff`);
  otherwise `UNIVERSE_UNAVAILABLE`.
- `timeframe` `5|15|60|1D|1W|1M`; `candles` 50-500; `density`
  `compact|comfortable|large|xlarge|xxlarge`; `pageSize` `6|12|18|24`;
  `paging` `pages|more`; `indicators` subset of `sma20`,`ema50`; `volume`.
- `sort`: `{field, direction}` with field `original`, `symbol`, `changePct`,
  `windowChangePct`, `volume`, `volumeRatio`, `value`.
- `filters`: partial merge of `query` (≤100 chars), `hideUnranked`, and
  numeric `changeMin`, `changeMax`, `volumeRatioMin`, `valueMin` (₹ Cr),
  `priceMin`, `priceMax`; `null` clears a threshold.
- `page` (1-based; in `more` mode it is how many pages are loaded),
  `linkTimeframe` (opening a card also applies the Grid timeframe to the chart),
  `refresh:true` (retry ranking and history).
- `chartIndicators`: `copy` captures the active chart's native indicators onto
  the cards (the "Use chart indicators" button; `CHART_INDICATORS_FAILED` if the
  chart changes or capture fails); `basic` returns to SMA/EMA overlays.
- `theme`: `app|dark|light|midnight|classic`.
- `width`: sidebar width in pixels (280-4096, clamped to the sidebar's
  min/max); not while expanded.
- `expanded`: enlarge the Grid over the workspace or return to the sidebar
  (refused in a narrow workspace).
- `openCard`: a symbol on the **current page** opens on the active chart
  (with the Grid timeframe when linked); `OPEN_CHART_FAILED` otherwise.
- `panel`: `close` closes the Grid, `openPage` opens it as a separate page
  (choose `chartIndicators:"basic"` first). Must be sent alone.

```json
{"type":"grid.configure","params":{"chartIndicators":"copy","theme":"dark","expanded":true},"idempotencyKey":"grid-look-001"}
```

Changing universe, sort, filters, pageSize or paging resets the page. Ranked
sorts and filters call the cloud ranking service; poll `grid.getState` while
`arrange.rankPending` or `loading` is true, and report `rankingError`/card
errors rather than hiding them.

### Boundaries

The per-card enlarge dialog remains interactive. The Grid's "Compare 2/4
charts" footer is not shown in the workspace Grid (no handler is wired there). Opening a card into the main
chart (UI or `openCard`) requires a ready cloud-backed `default` active chart
and ended replay; it never silently converts a broker/local chart.

# Chart command recipes and boundaries

Source-reviewed October 29, 2026. Discover each command on the intended Desktop
tab before using it. These recipes are not live-account or deployment proof.
Run CLI examples from `TradingLead-Desktop`, always with the explicit discovered
tab. JSON below is an executor envelope; CLI `--params`/`--params-file` takes
only its `params` object. Never send account, pane, grant or credential fields.
Unknown envelope/parameter keys are rejected.

## Context and permissions

1. Follow `tl-desktop` discovery; read `workspace.getState`, `chart.getState`
   and `feeds.list`. `available:true` on a feed describes its usable interface,
   not a verified authenticated provider session or fresh candles.
2. Verify the intended account and active pane, exact symbol/feed/interval and
   `dataReady:true` (widget `ready`, verified `history.state:"ready"`, settled
   discovery/source switching, no replay load). `ready:true` alone is not data.
   `chart.getState.data.error` is the active chart's error. A broker-catalog
   failure on the default feed is reported only in `data.feedCatalog`
   (`{state:"error",message}`); it blocks broker feeds, not the default chart.
   No chart command accepts `paneId`; select the target with `layout.set`
   `activePane` first (see [layouts-grid.md](layouts-grid.md)).
3. Use explicit `chart.open` parameters to change chart context, then poll state.
   It navigates the tab; it does not select Grid settings or a watchlist row.
4. Require the final `status:"ok"` and inspect domain state afterward.
   `requested:true,confirmed:false` is only acceptance.

All external commands require AI access. The catalog marks chart navigation,
reload/live and panel controls `mutates:false` despite their visible effects and
possible provider quota use. They do not require a retry key. Native study writes
require sign-in, indicator access and a retry key. Replay, view/compare/action,
drawings, layouts, Grid and drawing-template apply require sign-in, general local
write access and a retry key.
For an uncertain write, reconcile the same key and identical parameters; a timeout
is not rollback. Keys contain 1–80 letters/numbers/underscores/hyphens.

`feeds.list` discovers interfaces/capabilities, not provider login status,
entitlements, credentials or automatic fallback. Current source returns only the
default feed with `data.discovery.status:"error"` and code
`FEED_DISCOVERY_FAILED` when broker discovery fails, even though final command
`status` is `"ok"`. Inspect this nested status: no broker feed was verified, and
cached broker entries are not returned. `discovery.reason` is bounded:
`UNTRUSTED_ORIGIN`, `DESKTOP_INTERFACE_UNAVAILABLE`, `CATALOG_REJECTED`,
`CATALOG_CHANGED` or `UNKNOWN` (no raw error text). Successful discovery reports
`data.discovery.status:"ok"`.

Current source lets explicit `feed:"default"` calls to `chart.open` and
`marketData.getBars` proceed independently of broker discovery; requested provider
feeds still require successful discovery. This does not bypass default history
errors or select a fallback. These October 29 source corrections are not proof
that an installed tab has them: older handlers may still block default dispatch
or omit `discovery`. Report that distinction, not a successful broker discovery.

## Panels and bounded snapshot

```bash
tradinglead exec workspace.setPanel --tab ACTUAL_TAB_ID \
  --params '{"panel":"intelligence","expanded":true}'
```

```json
{"type":"chart.snapshot","params":{"bars":5}}
```

Send `expanded` explicitly for compatibility. Current source's shared command
adapter defaults omission to `true` and preserves explicit `false`; older
handlers may reject omission. This source correction is not installed-app proof.
Supported panel keys are
`peers`, `watchlists`, `futures`, `backtesting`, `paper-trading`, `intelligence`,
`indicators` (`simulation` is a legacy alias). Verify `workspace.getState.panels`.
This is not right-sidebar selection: use `workspace.openSidebar` (owned by
[tl-desktop](../tl-desktop/SKILL.md)) for Watch, Indices, Heatmap, Scan, Grid,
Patterns, Alerts, Research, Data Window, Paper and Contests. There is no generic
popup command.

Snapshot defaults to five trailing loaded rows, maximum 25, with bounded columns
and bytes. It does not fetch earlier history. Inspect schema, timestamps, missing
cells, truncation and calculation observations; study presence or a post-subscribe
data event is not proof of numerical correctness or an earlier error-free run.

Market Intelligence, Futures, Heatmap and other market-panel reads belong to
[tl-markets](../tl-markets/SKILL.md).

## Native studies and drawing templates

```json
{"type":"studies.list","params":{"offset":0,"limit":50}}
```

Use the returned exact name in `studies.inputs`, then apply only declared input
IDs/types/options/bounds with `studies.apply` and a unique key. Discovery pages
allow offset 0–10000 and limit 1–100. Inputs accept up to 64 declared primitive
values; strings are at most 200 characters. Do not guess a study name or input ID.

```json
{"type":"studies.applied","params":{"offset":0,"limit":50}}
```

For visibility/removal, copy the exact `entityId`, `name` and current boolean
`expectedVisible` from that response; `studies.setVisibility` also requires the
desired `visible`. Re-read on stale state. This targets unmanaged native studies
only, not TLScript/Python/backtest instances or drawings. Verify applied state
and snapshot values afterward; custom source/settings belong to their own skills.

Have the user select one editable drawing, then call `drawingTemplates.state`.
Use its exact `entityId` and `type` in `drawingTemplates.list` (nonnegative safe
integer offset, limit 1–50). Apply a returned exact `name` with those selectors
and a retry key. Recheck selection first. Apply changes style only; it creates or
deletes no drawing. Save/rename/delete/pin/last-used template behavior, drawing
creation/editing, full chart layouts and chart/style templates remain distinct
UI storage contracts, not invented commands. Native indicator templates use
`studyTemplates.manage` (see [SKILL.md](SKILL.md)).

## Native replay

```json
{"type":"chart.replayControl","params":{"action":"select"},"idempotencyKey":"native-select-001"}
```

The native notice/picker still requires a person to choose a candle. Poll
`chart.getState.replay`: verify `selecting:false`, a native cutoff, `runId:null`,
no loading/error and the intended context before playing or stepping.

```json
{"type":"chart.replayControl","params":{"action":"speed","speed":2},"idempotencyKey":"native-speed-001"}
```

```json
{"type":"chart.replayControl","params":{"action":"step"},"idempotencyKey":"native-step-001"}
```

Other supported actions are `play`, `pause`, `end`. Only `speed` accepts `speed`
(finite 0.1–200 bars/second); do not attach it to other actions. End is explicit
and restores ordinary chart history; it does not delete user studies/accounts.
Inspect cursor/loading/playing/error after requests. History navigation refuses
active replay rather than ending it. `chart.setReplayTime` is an internal
simulation integration, not a public manual-player command.

UI-only Back/Shift+Left is not a `back` replayControl action. Current shortcuts:
Shift+Space toggles; Shift+Right steps paused or temporarily boosts playing;
Shift+Up/Down changes speed with hold/release restoration. Escape cancels native
selection/help, not replay. Shortcuts route through registered workspace/native
documents to the active replay owner, or the remaining replay owner; typing,
composition, dialog/menu contexts and modifiers gate them. Do not promise
application-global keys or inactive-pane isolation based on key names.

Unmodified Space advances the displayed watchlist/index catalogue via its
registered navigation owner, not playback. It respects editing/overlay guards,
readiness and replay handoff prompts; it does not wrap at the last displayed row.
Arrow Up/Down in ticker rows changes selection through the displayed row order.
There is no public next-row/select-index/constituent-navigation command.
`universe.list` plus explicit `chart.open` is the available command workflow,
not parity with those UI selections.

Native replay reveals completed candles without strategy accounting. The UI
Trade handoff and paper orders/replay belong to `tl-paper-trading`; inspect
`runId` before choosing an owner. Never apply native end-of-candle clock semantics
to a simulation cutoff or claim native commands fill orders.

## Saved alerts

Saved price alerts (`alerts.*`) moved to [tl-alerts](../tl-alerts/SKILL.md).

## Intentional manual and administrative boundaries

Chart Grid is a separate cloud-backed gallery, not split chart layouts or
Historical Patterns; its commands are in [layouts-grid.md](layouts-grid.md).
Opening a card from the UI requires a ready cloud-backed `default` active chart
and explicitly ended replay; it never silently converts a broker/local chart.
Ranking uses stored summaries while cards use loaded bars; values can differ.
Only the per-card enlarge dialog remains UI-only.

Chart/popup property editing beyond `chart.setView`, toolbar visibility, native
OHLC legend collapse, favorite drawing-tool membership, crosshair sync between
panes, drawing styles beyond templates, and saved-layout rename/delete remain
user-only. Shift+F is a guarded fullscreen UI shortcut; use
`chart.action` fullscreen or `layout.set` fullscreen instead. Do not synthesize
arbitrary JavaScript or keyboard events to fake API coverage. Account-local
layout storage and synced panel/replay preferences are different contracts;
source presence does not prove cloud-rule deployment.

Sign-in, broker OAuth/token renewal, grant approval, subscription/paywall checkout
and account administration are human-owned flows, not chart commands. Chat
configuration and historical data repair are separate owner/admin operations;
`chart.reload`/history retry does not repair stored candles. Do not invent
auth/billing/admin/repair namespaces, reset account state, or launch/reload the
app to work around an unavailable tab.

---
name: tl-markets
description: Read and operate TradingLead market panels through discovered commands. Use for watchlists (Watch sidebar grid rows/sort/filter/columns/search, CSV text export, manual row order, row flags, favorite-star lists, selecting lists or rows, creating, adding/removing symbols, renaming/deleting cloud watchlists), Multi Watchlists, symbol company details, peers and peer refresh, published indices and constituents, the market heatmap, Market Intelligence and Futures reports, stock universes/categories and raw OHLCV candles via marketData.getBars. Chart drawing/layout belongs to tl-charts; scanner runs to tl-screening; alerts to tl-alerts.
---

# TradingLead markets: watchlists and market panels

Start with [tl-desktop](../tl-desktop/SKILL.md) for connection, grants and
retries. Exact fields: [commands.md](commands.md). Discover each command on
the intended tab; source support does not prove an installed app has it.

Most of these commands drive a **mounted panel** in the current account's
`/charts` workspace. Open the panel first, poll `workspace.getState`, then use
the command. `MARKET_NOT_READY` means the panel is not mounted for that
account; `MARKET_LOADING` means wait and reread.

| Panel | Open with | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Watch (right sidebar) | `workspace.openSidebar {"panel":"watchlists"}` | `watchlists.getRows/select/setView/removeSymbols/manage` |
| Symbol details (Watch sidebar Details) | Watch sidebar | `symbol.details` |
| Indices (right sidebar) | `workspace.openSidebar {"panel":"indices"}` | `indices.getState` |
| Heatmap (right sidebar) | `workspace.openSidebar {"panel":"heatmap"}` | `heatmap.getState/configure` |
| Peers (bottom tab) | `workspace.setPanel {"panel":"peers","expanded":true}` | `peers.get/configure` |
| Multi Watchlists (bottom tab) | `workspace.setPanel {"panel":"watchlists","expanded":true}` | `watchlists.multiView` |
| Market Intelligence (bottom tab) | `workspace.setPanel {"panel":"intelligence","expanded":true}` | `intelligence.catalog/getReport` |
| Futures (bottom tab) | `workspace.setPanel {"panel":"futures","expanded":true}` | `futures.getReport` |
| No panel | — | `watchlists.list/create/addSymbols`, `universe.list`, `marketData.getBars` |

**Grants.** `symbol.details`, `indices.getState`, `watchlists.multiView` are
grant-free reads when their change parameter is omitted; pagination is read-only.
Supplying `expanded`, `category` or `panels`, respectively (including false/empty),
requires the general write grant, sign-in and a retry key;
`peers.configure` is a separate mutating refresh so `peers.get` stays a plain read.
Read-only (no key): `watchlists.getRows`, `watchlists.list`, `peers.get`,
`heatmap.getState`, `intelligence.*`, `futures.getReport`, `universe.list`,
`marketData.getBars`. Every mutating `watchlists.*` command (including
`select`, `setView` and `multiView`) needs a **real signed-in account**; the local
development preview fails with `REAL_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED`. Missing grants return
`APPROVAL_REQUIRED`; agents cannot grant themselves access.
An uncertain or cancelled write may have persisted: inspect before retrying and
never issue a fresh key automatically.

## Watch grid

```json
{"type":"watchlists.getRows","params":{"offset":0,"limit":25}}
```

Returns `activeList`, a page of rows (`symbol` plus up to 24 column values),
`total`, `truncated`, column state (`colId`, hide, width, pinned, sort), filter
model, quick-search text and the favorite-starred lists/categories
(`favorites`). It addresses only the **primary Watch grid**;
quotes are shared summaries, not verified fresh market data. Read column IDs
here before `setView`.

**CSV text.** `{"format":"csv","offset":0,"limit":100,"columns":["EXACT_COL_ID"]}`
returns `{csv, bytes, shown, total, columns, truncated, columnsTruncated}` for
the displayed (filtered and sorted) rows of that page, using the grid's own
exporter. `columns` (CSV only, 1-24) must be visible column IDs; default is the
first 24 visible. Cells starting with `= + - @` or a tab/newline are prefixed
with `'` (`spreadsheetFormulaEscaping:true`). Over 128 KiB fails
`EXPORT_TOO_LARGE`: lower `limit` or columns. Nothing is written to a file or
the clipboard; page with `offset` for more rows.

### Select a list or a row

```json
{"type":"watchlists.select","params":{"kind":"watchlist","name":"Swing"},"idempotencyKey":"watch-select-001"}
```

Send `kind` (`category|watchlist|flaglist`) with an exact existing `name`,
**or** `symbol` (a ticker currently visible in `getRows`), not both. If the
Watch grid has applied screener filters, switching lists fails with
`CONFIRM_REQUIRED` unless you pass `clearFilters:true`, which discards them;
only do that when the user agreed. Selecting a row requests the chart switch
(`chartSelectionRequested:true,dataReady:false`); poll `chart.getState`.
Selecting a list returns `loading:true`; reread rows. `SYMBOL_NOT_VISIBLE` means
the ticker is not in the current filtered/sorted view.

### Sort, filter, columns and search

```json
{"type":"watchlists.setView","params":{"sort":[{"colId":"EXACT_COL_ID","sort":"desc"}],"search":"BANK"},"idempotencyKey":"watch-view-001"}
```

- `sort`: up to 12 `{colId, sort: asc|desc}` in priority order; `[]` clears.
- `filters`: AG Grid text/number/set models keyed by column ID, up to two
  conditions joined by AND/OR; `{}` clears. `FILTER_UNAVAILABLE` means that
  column has no installed filter in this build.
- `columns`: up to 24 `{colId, hide?, width?, pinned?}` in display order.
  UI-locked columns reject hide/pin/width changes.
- `search`: quick filter, at most 80 characters; empty clears.
- `move`: `{symbol, toIndex}` sent **alone** moves one existing row in the
  list's manual order, the same writer as drag-and-drop. Clear sort, column
  filters and search first (`ORDER_VIEW_CONFLICT`; applied screeners also block
  it). Returns `{symbol, toIndex, changed, persisted:true}` after reading the
  saved order back. `ORDER_NOT_PERSISTED` is not rollback: read rows before
  retrying with the same key.

Column layout persists as the user's preference; filters and search are
session-only. The result is a fresh `getRows`-style read; `VIEW_NOT_APPLIED`
means nothing was applied.

## Cloud watchlists

```json
{"type":"watchlists.list","params":{}}
```

```json
{"type":"watchlists.create","params":{"name":"Breakouts June","symbols":["NSE:TCS-EQ","NSE:INFY-EQ"]},"idempotencyKey":"watch-create-001"}
```

1. Read `watchlists.list` and verify a real signed-in account. These are
   TradingLead watchlists, not broker watchlists.
2. Require the user's separate write grant (**Allow AI watchlist and
   saved-screener changes**). Local automatic access is not that grant.
3. `watchlists.create` / `watchlists.addSymbols` take `symbols` **or** a
   completed legacy `screener.run` job's `runId`, not both. That `runId` is
   only that job service, not `screening.*`, persisted history or `patterns.*`.
   For Scanner selections, collect explicit tickers via
   [tl-screening](../tl-screening/SKILL.md). Writes accept at most 500 symbols;
   do not silently drop or split without reviewing scope. `create` never
   overwrites an existing different list.
4. Remove members with `watchlists.removeSymbols {name, symbols}`: 1-100 unique
   tickers that are actual members (`SYMBOL_NOT_IN_LIST` otherwise); chunk larger
   removals.
5. Rename or delete with `watchlists.manage`:

```json
{"type":"watchlists.manage","params":{"action":"rename","name":"Swing","newName":"Swing 2026"},"idempotencyKey":"watch-rename-001"}
```

   `delete` requires `confirm:true` and is irreversible; only delete a list the
   user named explicitly. `removeSymbols`/`manage` need the Watch sidebar
   mounted. Reread `watchlists.list` or `getRows` afterwards.
6. Favorite star a list or category (pinned at the top of the list selector):

```json
{"type":"watchlists.manage","params":{"action":"favorite","kind":"watchlist","name":"Swing","enabled":true},"idempotencyKey":"watch-fav-001"}
```

   Desired-state: already matching is a no-op. Check `getRows.favorites`.
7. Flag visible rows with a colour (flag lists):

```json
{"type":"watchlists.manage","params":{"action":"flag","symbols":["NSE:TCS-EQ"],"color":"red"},"idempotencyKey":"watch-flag-001"}
```

   1-100 unique tickers that are **visible** in the Watch grid
   (`SYMBOL_NOT_VISIBLE` otherwise); colours `red|blue|green|yellow|purple|cyan|pink`,
   `currentColor` removes the flag. Flags are written one symbol at a time and a
   failure can leave earlier symbols flagged; reread before retrying. Wait out
   `MARKET_LOADING` while another watchlist write is running.

## Symbol details and peers

`symbol.details` reads the current **chart** symbol's company panel (sector,
industry, about, up to 20 key points, 30 ratios, 10 news titles) with state
`unsupported|collapsed|loading|error|empty|ready`. It never takes a symbol: use
`chart.open` or `watchlists.select` first. `expanded:true` opens Details; then
poll without `expanded` until `ready`. A collapsed panel is not fetched. Data
is a stored upstream snapshot, not verified live fundamentals.

```json
{"type":"symbol.details","params":{"expanded":true},"idempotencyKey":"details-open-001"}
```

`peers.get {"limit":25}` (1-100) returns the current chart symbol's `matched`
peers (linked to chart tickers) and `unmatched` entries, `total`, `truncated`
and stored provenance. Unmatched peers are not chart symbols; do not invent
tickers for them. `peers.get` never refetches.

```json
{"type":"peers.configure","params":{"refresh":true},"idempotencyKey":"peers-refresh-001"}
```

`peers.configure {"refresh":true}` does exactly what the Peers Refresh/Retry
button does: reloads the stored peer data and chart catalog for the current
symbol and returns `state:"loading", refreshRequested:true`. Poll `peers.get`
until it settles. It does not scrape upstream sources.

## Multi Watchlists

```json
{"type":"watchlists.multiView","params":{},"idempotencyKey":"multi-read-001"}
```

Returns current panels (max 12), `available` existing lists, `storageError`.
Passing `panels: [{type, name}]` replaces the layout with existing lists of
the current account (`WATCHLIST_NOT_FOUND` otherwise); `[]` closes all cards but
never deletes lists. The layout is device/account-local. Requires a retry key
even to read.

## Indices

```json
{"type":"indices.getState","params":{"offset":0,"limit":25},"idempotencyKey":"indices-read-001"}
```

Without `category`, returns the published index catalog (category, ticker,
label, member count) and the selected index's constituents with paging.
`category` selects a published index **and opens its index ticker on the
chart** (`chartSelectionRequested:true`); reread to get its constituents.
`INDEX_NOT_AVAILABLE` means it is not published or still loading.

## Heatmap

```json
{"type":"heatmap.getState","params":{}}
```

Reads settings, aggregate breadth and quote receipt time, not per-ticker
quotes; receipt time is not provider freshness.

```json
{"type":"heatmap.configure","params":{"universe":"EXACT_OFFERED_ID","sizeMode":"turnover","groupBy":"sector"},"idempotencyKey":"heatmap-config-001"}
```

`universe` must be an offered ID (the configure result lists up to 100
`universes`; `UNIVERSE_NOT_AVAILABLE` otherwise). `sizeMode`
`turnover|volume|percent|equal` (`percent` sizes by absolute daily move;
`turnover` is a traded-value proxy, not market cap), `groupBy` `sector|none`,
`colorScale` `2|3|5|10`, `limit` `0|50|100|250|500`, `search` (highlight,
≤80 chars), `expanded`. The result is `viewChangeRequested:true`; poll
`heatmap.getState`. **Historical periods are unsupported**: the heatmap only
has current quotes (no time series or period returns), so do not ask for or
invent a 1W/1M view. The heatmap error Retry button is UI-only.

## Market Intelligence and Futures

After opening Intelligence, read `intelligence.catalog` (up to 50 authorized
published reports and filters) and use an exact discovered dataset with
`intelligence.getReport` (at most 10 rows, optional `symbol`/`date`, snapshot
provenance). `futures.getReport` returns at most five published NSE participant
summaries (`isIndex` true by default).

```json
{"type":"futures.getReport","params":{"isIndex":true}}
```

These are mounted, authorized published-report reads, not analysis execution,
live positions, streaming quotes or evidence of redistribution rights.

## Universes and raw candles

`universe.list` lists stock categories, or with `category` the symbols in one.

`marketData.getBars` reads OHLCV candles without moving the chart, through the
same feed path the chart uses for the named feed. Pick the feed with
`feeds.list` (owned by [tl-charts](../tl-charts/SKILL.md)); give `from`+`to`,
`to`+`countBack`, or `countBack` (≤5000 bars; `time` is epoch ms UTC). It never
substitutes a feed; the result is history, not a live quote. For `default`,
the transport may be Desktop-local or cloud-routed; the response does not name
the transport, so inspect candle times and report unverified provenance and
freshness rather than certifying them.

```json
{"type":"marketData.getBars","params":{"feed":"kite","symbol":"NSE:RELIANCE-EQ","resolution":"5","from":"2024-01-10","to":"2024-01-12"}}
```

## UI-only

File/clipboard export and list import dialogs, broker watchlists, the Heatmap
Retry button, heatmap historical periods and the secondary Multi/Indices/Peers
grids' own rows/sort/filter state have no commands (`watchlists.getRows`
addresses only the primary Watch grid). Do not fake them with
arbitrary JavaScript.

# tl-markets command reference

Source-only snapshot from an isolated frontend registry; installed Desktop execution is not certified. Rediscover live availability before use.
Use explicit tab targeting and inspect the final JSON status. Do not guess IDs or grant permissions.

Do not infer grant permissions from `mutates`: Desktop discovery can omit structured grant metadata. Read [tl-desktop](../tl-desktop/SKILL.md) for the verified local-change versus cloud-watchlist access rules.

## `watchlists.getRows`

Read displayed Watch rows/state or bounded formula-safe CSV text; no file/clipboard writes or freshness claim.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **none**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `offset` | 0-100000, default 0 |
| `limit` | 1-100, default 25 |
| `format` | rows (default)\|csv; CSV <=128 KiB |
| `columns` | CSV only: 1-24 visible column IDs; default visible columns |

## `watchlists.select`

Select a discovered list OR visible row on the active chart. Mounted Watch required; poll rows/chart.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **navigate, quota, network, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `kind` | category\|watchlist\|flaglist; with name |
| `name` | Exact list ID |
| `symbol` | Visible row ticker; instead of kind/name |
| `clearFilters` | Explicit true to discard applied screeners on list switch |

## `watchlists.setView`

Set mounted Watch sort/filter/column state. Existing column preferences persist; filters are session-only.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **panel, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `sort` | Up to 12 {colId,sort:asc\|desc}; [] clears |
| `filters` | AG text/number/set by column ID; two-condition AND/OR; {} clears |
| `columns` | Up to 24 {colId,hide?,width?,pinned?}, in order |
| `search` | Optional quick-filter text, <=80 chars; empty clears |
| `move` | Exclusive {symbol,toIndex}: move an existing row in unfiltered, unsorted manual order |

## `watchlists.removeSymbols`

Remove 1-100 symbols from an existing cloud watchlist using the UI writer.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **network, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Existing watchlist |
| `symbols` | 1-100 unique canonical tickers |

## `watchlists.manage`

Manage lists/favorite stars or flag visible rows using guarded UI stores. Delete requires confirm:true.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **panel, network, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `action` | rename\|delete\|favorite\|flag |
| `name` | Existing list/category; not for flag |
| `newName` | Rename only |
| `confirm` | Delete only: true |
| `kind` | Favorite only: watchlist\|category |
| `enabled` | Favorite only: required boolean |
| `symbols` | Flag only: 1-100 unique visible tickers |
| `color` | Flag only: red\|blue\|green\|yellow\|purple\|cyan\|pink\|currentColor (remove) |

## `symbol.details`

Read bounded mounted company/fundamentals without a write grant; expanded changes require write approval and a retry key. No automatic fetch while collapsed.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **panel, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `expanded` | Optional boolean; poll after opening |

## `peers.get`

Read up to 100 matched/unmatched peers for the mounted Peers panel's current chart symbol.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **none**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `limit` | 1-100, default 25 |

## `peers.configure`

Reload mounted peers through the UI Refresh/Retry path; poll peers.get. Does not scrape upstream.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **network, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `refresh` | Required true; reload stored peers and chart catalog |

## `indices.getState`

Read index catalog/constituents without a write grant; category selection requires write approval and a retry key and opens its index on chart.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **navigate, write, quota, network**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `category` | Optional published category ID |
| `offset` | 0-100000, default 0 |
| `limit` | 1-100, default 25 |

## `heatmap.configure`

Configure mounted heatmap using its offered universe/options; no historical period exists. Poll getState.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **panel, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `universe` | Exact offered universe ID |
| `sizeMode` | turnover\|volume\|percent\|equal |
| `groupBy` | sector\|none |
| `colorScale` | 2\|3\|5\|10 |
| `limit` | 0\|50\|100\|250\|500 |
| `search` | Optional highlight query, <=80 chars |
| `expanded` | Optional boolean |

## `watchlists.multiView`

Read mounted Multi Watchlists without a write grant; panels replacement requires write approval and a retry key.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **panel, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `panels` | Optional array of {type:category\|watchlist\|flaglist,name}; [] closes all cards |

## `intelligence.catalog`

Read up to 50 authorized published report names and filter availability from the open Market Intelligence panel. Not streaming quotes.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **network**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

Parameters: `{}`.

## `intelligence.getReport`

Read at most 10 authorized published report rows with snapshot provenance. Requires the mounted panel and a dataset from intelligence.catalog; not live quotes or redistribution rights.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **network**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `dataset` | Exact available dataset from intelligence.catalog. |
| `symbol` | Optional supported canonical symbol filter. |
| `date` | Optional YYYY-MM-DD snapshot date. |

## `futures.getReport`

Read at most five published NSE participant summaries from the mounted Futures panel. Aggregate reports, not live positions or forecasts.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **network**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `isIndex` | Optional boolean, true for index futures (default), false for stock futures. |

## `heatmap.getState`

Read current heatmap settings, aggregate breadth and quote receipt time from the open panel. No per-ticker quotes; receipt time is not provider freshness.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **none**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

Parameters: `{}`.

## `marketData.getBars`

Fetch historical OHLCV candles for a symbol/interval/window through the exact same feed path the chart uses. Pick the feed with feeds.list (default TradingLead/local adapters, or a connected broker like kite, fyers, web-dhan). Give the window as from+to, to+countBack, or just countBack. Returns up to 5000 bounded candles with epoch-millisecond UTC times; not a live/streaming quote and receipt time is not provider freshness. No feed is ever silently substituted.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **quota, network**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `feed` | Feed id from feeds.list (e.g. default, kite, fyers, web-dhan). |
| `symbol` | Canonical ticker in the feed's format, e.g. NSE:RELIANCE-EQ. |
| `resolution` | Whole minutes 1-1440 (including 3,10,20,45,75,90), or 1D,1W,1M. Broker custom intervals require a compatible exact-divisor native base; no provider substitution. |
| `from` | Optional window start: YYYY-MM-DD or epoch seconds. Supply from and/or countBack. |
| `to` | Optional window end: YYYY-MM-DD or epoch seconds; defaults to now. |
| `countBack` | Optional number of candles ending at 'to' (1-5000). Supply from and/or countBack. |

## `universe.list`

List available stock categories or the symbols in one category.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **network**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `category` | Optional category identifier from this command. |

## `watchlists.list`

List the signed-in user's TradingLead watchlists, not broker watchlists.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **network**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

Parameters: `{}`.

## `watchlists.create`

Create a TradingLead watchlist without overwriting an existing different list. Requires sign-in, an idempotencyKey and local write permission for external agents.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **network, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Watchlist name |
| `symbols` | Canonical ticker array; supply symbols OR runId. |
| `runId` | Completed scan to save; supply runId OR symbols. |

## `watchlists.addSymbols`

Add unique symbols to an existing TradingLead watchlist. Requires sign-in, an idempotencyKey and local write permission for external agents.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **network, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Existing watchlist name |
| `symbols` | Canonical ticker array; supply symbols OR runId. |
| `runId` | Completed scan to save; supply runId OR symbols. |

---
name: tl-alerts
description: Manage TradingLead saved price alerts through discovered commands. Use to list saved alert rules, create horizontal price alerts with an optional trigger message and expiry, edit name/price/direction/price source/frequency/message/expiry, pause/resume, delete, and read persisted trigger activity history; also explains when alerts are actually monitored. Not chart drawings (tl-charts), not broker orders and not push notifications.
---

# TradingLead saved price alerts

Start with [tl-desktop](../tl-desktop/SKILL.md) for connection, grants and
retries. Exact fields: [commands.md](commands.md). Discover the commands on the
intended tab before use. The **Alerts** right-sidebar panel is
`workspace.openSidebar {"panel":"alerts"}`.

## What an alert is, and when it is monitored

Rules are saved per account in the cloud. Monitoring is **client-side**: rules
are evaluated against shared cloud quotes only while the signed-in account's
Alerts panel is mounted in an open TradingLead tab. Saving a rule does not
create always-on server monitoring, push delivery, broker-feed identity or
order execution. Quotes carry receipt time, not market timestamps. After
changing rules externally, a mounted Alerts panel may need reopening to pick up
the edit. Never promise that an alert will fire.

**Expiry follows the same rule.** A rule past its `expiresAt` is shown as
*Expired* and is no longer subscribed or evaluated, but only a mounted Alerts
panel enforces this; the stored rule keeps `status:"active"` (`alerts.list`
reports `expired:true` alongside). There are no OS, desktop, sound or push
notifications: the optional `message` appears in the in-app Live trigger card.

> **Deployment caveat (message/expiry).** Support for `message` and
> `expiresAt` needs an Alerts API schema change that is **not yet deployed**.
> Until it is, production rejects any create/update that includes either field
> with `ALERT_INVALID_REQUEST` (400); rules without them are unaffected. If you
> get that error, retry without these fields only after telling the user.

## Commands

| Command | Writes | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alerts.list` | no | Saved rules: id, name, ticker, timeframe, status, type, direction, detail, price source, frequency, revision, plus `message`, `expiresAt` and `expired` when set. Not trigger state. |
| `alerts.activity` | no | One page of persisted cloud trigger events, newest first. |
| `alerts.create` | yes | New horizontal latest-price rule. |
| `alerts.update` | yes | Edit fields of an existing rule. |
| `alerts.setEnabled` | yes | Pause (`false`) or resume (`true`). |
| `alerts.delete` | yes | Delete the rule (not any chart drawing). |

Writes need sign-in, the general **write** grant (`allowAgentWrites`) and a
unique retry key. Missing grant: `APPROVAL_REQUIRED`; agents cannot grant it.
IDs are 1-128 letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens, copied from
`alerts.list`. Updates, toggles and deletes fetch the latest saved version and
write with its etag; they take no `etag`/`expectedRevision`. Resolve
`ALERT_CONFLICT` by rereading (and reopening the panel if needed), never by
blind overwrite. An uncertain write may have persisted: reread before retrying
with the same key.

## Create

```json
{"type":"alerts.list","params":{}}
```

```json
{"type":"alerts.create","params":{"ticker":"NSE:TCS-EQ","price":4000,"direction":"above","timeframe":"1D","frequency":"once"},"idempotencyKey":"alert-create-001"}
```

This example is not investment advice; create rules only when the user asked
and confirmed ticker and level. `ticker` is 1-64 letters/numbers/`:_.-`;
`price` is finite with absolute value ≤1e15; `direction`
`above|below|either|touch` (default `above`); `timeframe` a resolution like
`1`, `15`, `1D` (default `1D`, used for bar bucketing); `frequency`
`once|once_per_bar|every_cross` (default `once`); optional `name` 1-160
characters; optional `message` (1-500 characters, single line, no control
characters) and `expiresAt` (a **future** ISO UTC time
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.ffffff]Z`, e.g. `2026-12-31T09:15:00Z`; monitoring stops
after it). Created rules use the `last` price source and synthetic `default`
feed metadata. Trendline alerts must be drawn on the chart by a person.

## Edit

```json
{"type":"alerts.update","params":{"id":"EXACT_RULE_ID","price":4100,"frequency":"once_per_bar"},"idempotencyKey":"alert-update-001"}
```

Send `id` plus at least one of `name`, `price`, `direction`, `priceSource`
(`last|close|wick`), `frequency`, `message` (`""` clears) or `expiresAt`
(future ISO UTC; `null` clears; a new future time un-expires the rule). `price` applies only to horizontal rules;
on a trendline rule it fails with `ALERT_GEOMETRY_UNSUPPORTED` (move the line on
the chart instead). An edit equal to the saved rule returns `unchanged:true`
without writing. There are no notification-channel or ticker/timeframe
fields; do not invent them.

```json
{"type":"alerts.update","params":{"id":"EXACT_RULE_ID","message":"Check volume before entry","expiresAt":"2026-12-31T09:15:00Z"},"idempotencyKey":"alert-msg-001"}
```

```json
{"type":"alerts.setEnabled","params":{"id":"EXACT_RULE_ID","enabled":false},"idempotencyKey":"alert-pause-001"}
```

`alerts.delete {"id": ...}` removes the rule permanently; delete only rules the
user named. Reread `alerts.list` after every write.

## Trigger activity

```json
{"type":"alerts.activity","params":{"limit":20}}
```

Optional `ruleId`, `limit` 1-50 (default 20) and `cursor` from the previous
page. Each event has `id`, `ruleId`, `ruleRevision`, `eventType`, `detectedAt`,
`candleTime`, `price`, `level` and `acrossGap`; follow `cursor` until `null`
for a complete history. These are persisted cloud events, not the panel's live
in-memory monitor state. An empty page means no persisted events, not that
monitoring is running or that the price never crossed.

## UI-only

Drawing or dragging trendline alerts and reading the panel's live in-memory
activity view are interactive only. Server-side expiry enforcement and
out-of-app notifications do not exist.

# tl-alerts command reference

Source-only snapshot from an isolated frontend registry; installed Desktop execution is not certified. Rediscover live availability before use.
Use explicit tab targeting and inspect the final JSON status. Do not guess IDs or grant permissions.

Do not infer grant permissions from `mutates`: Desktop discovery can omit structured grant metadata. Read [tl-desktop](../tl-desktop/SKILL.md) for the verified local-change versus cloud-watchlist access rules.

## `alerts.list`

List this account's saved cloud chart alert rules (id, ticker, timeframe, status, direction, price/trendline, frequency, price source). Read-only; does not return live trigger state.

Retry key: **not required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **network**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

Parameters: `{}`.

## `alerts.create`

Create a horizontal latest-price alert on a symbol, monitored from shared cloud quotes while the signed-in Alerts panel is mounted. Trendline alerts must be drawn on the chart. Requires sign-in, local write permission and an idempotencyKey.

Retry key: **required**. External local-assistant access is still required.
Effects: **network, write**. These are possible consequences, not grants; optional write variants still require approval and a retry key.

| Parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `ticker` | Canonical ticker, e.g. NSE:TCS-EQ |
| `price` | Finite price level to cross |
| `direction` | Optional above\|below\|either\|touch, default above |
| `timeframe` | Optional resolution for bar bucketing, e.g. 1, 15, 1D; default 1D |
| `frequency` | Optional once\|once_per_bar\|every_cross, default once |
| `name` | Optional label |
| `message` | Optional trigger note, max 500 |
| `expiresAt` | Optional future ISO UTC; stops monitoring after |

---
name: tl-screening
description: Operate the unified TradingLead Scanner (Scan sidebar), original strategies, custom conditions and SQL; inspect/filter/sort/select the real results grid, refine stocks into another scan, reopen Scanned History, reuse saved screener rules and hand results to Chart Grid or a cloud watchlist. Also routes legacy jobs and local broker TLScript-Pine indicator scans. Watchlist management itself belongs to tl-markets.

# Screening (Scan sidebar)

Start with [tl-desktop](../tl-desktop/SKILL.md). Read
[commands.md](commands.md) and discover the chosen screening surface before
constructing a request.

`mutates:false` is a command grant/retry classification, **not** a promise of
no effects: opening/configuring changes the visible workspace, and running
consumes account/provider allowance and may persist a completed scan in history.
These actions still need external assistant access and real service authorization.
They have no write retry receipt; inspect state after an uncertain start instead
of automatically starting another chargeable run.

## Choose the data source explicitly

| Workflow | Discovery | Execution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unified visible Scanner: presets, original strategies, custom rules, SQL | `screening.getState`, `screening.catalog`, `screening.listUniverses` | `screening.configure`, `screening.run`, `screening.getResults` |
| Existing separate backend strategy jobs (not the visible Scanner) | `screener.listCapabilities`, `universe.list` | `screener.run` |
| Local provider candles + bounded TLScript-Pine indicator | `providerScreener.listCapabilities`, `feeds.list` | `providerScreener.run` |

For one ticker across historical weekdays/time windows, use
[tl-patterns](../tl-patterns/SKILL.md), not a Scanner SQL
workaround. The `patterns.*` commands own that separate sidebar.

Changing a chart to Kite/Fyers does **not** change backend screening to that
provider. Local Python indicators do not automatically become backend filters.
Provider connections and interval support depend on the addressed Desktop
tab; browser feed availability is a different surface. A listed provider is
not proof that its data is connected, entitled or fresh.

## Unified visible Scanner

### Authentication and fixture boundaries

The current website Scanner requires real sign-in. Older sample/development
branches and deterministic browser fixtures are not evidence that the addressed
app offers a login-free preview. Inspect its actual state and capabilities;
never substitute sample data for failed account/API access.

Use the `screening.*` family for actions the user should see in the Scan sidebar.
These commands call the same controller and API as its buttons, not a parallel
hidden scanner. Cloud requires real sign-in.
Open `/charts` first. `screening.getState` connects the visible **Scanner** and
returns its draft revision, current view, stage summaries and pending refinement.
`getState` and `show` reopen an already-mounted hidden Scanner; result polling
does not repeatedly force the sidebar open.
Discover the server catalog and available lists. An older running reader may
offer presets/SQL but not strategy endpoints or history, even when source code
has been updated. Do not silently substitute another backend or restart services.

1. Read `screening.getState`, `screening.catalog` and `screening.listUniverses`.
2. Send `screening.configure` with a complete advertised definition and that
   `expectedRevision`. Optional `universe` selects `active`, named `watchlist`,
   `flag`, `category`, or explicit unique canonical `symbols`.
3. Read state again after the UI update. Confirm the definition and list count,
   then call `screening.run` with the new revision. Configuring never runs.
4. Poll `screening.getResults` with the returned `runId`. Paginate using
   `nextOffset`; default 10 and maximum 25 rows per command. Check status,
   warnings, coverage counts and server truncation. Detailed coverage stays in
   the UI. Live run handles and combined comparison chains are tab-only; an
   updated backend separately persists individual scans. Inspect `meta.history`
   instead of assuming every successful scan was saved.
5. Use `screening.cancel` to stop this run. Closing Scan or changing the list
   cancels pending requests. Cancellation targets only the matching running
   query, not completed snapshots or unrelated saves. Already-submitted work
   can still consume allowance. Completed results stay readable while editing
   the next setup; auxiliary allowance-refresh warnings do not cancel them.

Example definition (substitute the revision returned by the addressed tab;
verify the advertised fields and your account permissions first):

```json
{
  "type": "screening.configure",
  "params": {
    "expectedRevision": 1,
    "definition": {
      "mode": "custom",
      "timeframe": "1D",
      "lookback_days": 180,
      "limit": 50,
      "match": "all",
      "conditions": [
        {"field": "close", "op": "gt", "value_field": "sma20"},
        {"field": "rsi14", "op": "lt", "value": 70}
      ]
    },
    "universe": {"kind": "symbols", "tickers": ["NSE:TCS-EQ", "NSE:INFY-EQ"]}
  }
}
```

Presets, nested AND/OR conditions and privileged read-only SQL use the server
contract. SQL access is server-granted, never inferred from an agent's role.
Account execution, lookback, ticker, concurrency and saved-library limits apply
equally to UI and command runs. Do not silently split an oversized list into
extra chargeable scans. Source data can have unresolved split/bonus defects;
report the warning rather than interpreting every price jump as a signal.

For a daily gain of at least 4% from the previous observed close, discover
`gainers` and its parameters, then configure a preset definition with
`mode:"preset"`, `preset:"gainers"`, `timeframe:"1D"` and
`parameters:{"min_change_pct":4,"change_basis":"previous_close"}`.
Use `"open"` only when the user means gain from that candle's open. Discover
the permitted lookback/limit and universe, and follow the same revision/run/poll
sequence above. This screens the latest stored eligible bar per ticker, not
live percentage movers; inspect returned dates and warnings before calling it
today's result. It does not find every historical day with a 4% move.

For Custom SQL, first verify `screening.catalog.capabilities.permissions.sql`
and its advertised `sql` schema. A supported daily definition uses
`mode:"sql"`, `timeframe:"1D"`, permitted `lookback_days`/`limit`, and
`sql:"SELECT ticker, datetime, close FROM ticker_summary_daily ORDER BY close DESC"`.
Use that table only if the addressed catalog advertises it. Select unqualified
physical table/column names, not calculated rule fields such as `rsi14` or
`sma20`. The server scopes every physical read to the selected stocks, timeframe
and dates; changing timeframe does not rewrite SQL table names. SQL completion
and the copy/paste AI prompt are UI assistance, not a validation or execution
bypass. Review any generated SQL before the explicit run.

### Original strategies in the same Scanner

Discover `screening.catalog.strategiesCatalog.screeners` and their parameter
types/defaults. A `strategiesCatalogError` is an explicit discovery failure, not
an empty successful strategy registry. Use `mode:"classic"` with
`screeners:[{name,parameters}]`; do not send UI `enabled` flags or a pipeline.
Up to five distinct parameter instances may be combined. Original algorithms
are not interchangeable with similarly named presets.
The Classic strategy named **Patterns Filter** is one of those multi-stock
rules, not the separate single-ticker Historical Patterns sidebar.

```json
{
  "type": "screening.configure",
  "params": {
    "expectedRevision": 1,
    "definition": {
      "mode": "classic",
      "screeners": [
        {"name": "KernelRegressionStrategy", "parameters": {"timeframe": "1D"}}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Substitute a currently discovered name, valid parameters and actual revision.
`getResults.data` contains raw per-stock rule results/errors for Classic.
These are **evaluated rows**, not necessarily matches. Signals remain
rule-defined: `1` is not universally bullish; zero, negative, null and failed
instances are distinct. Successful sibling rules survive partial failures.

### Analyse and refine through the real grid

1. Wait for the current run to complete. Call `screening.getAnalysis` with its
   `runId`; page columns using `columnOffset/columnLimit` and filtered rows with
   `offset/limit`. Use returned column IDs, never guessed SQL field names.
   Row values are projected to the returned column page; traverse both
   paginations for a complete comparison. Reduce page sizes if
   `RESULT_TOO_LARGE` is returned rather than treating omitted data as zero.
2. `screening.setAnalysis` takes that `runId` and `expectedAnalysisRevision`.
   It controls the same search, typed filters, sorting, hidden columns,
   selection and expanded analysis the user sees. Arrays replace the
   corresponding state; omitted fields stay unchanged. `reset:true` is
   exclusive. Invalid requests must not partially change the grid.
   Up to 20 filters are supported, including two AND conditions on the same
   discovered column for a lower/upper range; values must match its type.
3. Read analysis again after a display change. Read `screening.getState` for
   the current draft revision, then call `screening.refine` with both revisions,
   `runId` and `scope:"filtered"` or `"selected"`.
4. Refinement captures real grid-filtered stocks across **all pages**; hidden
   selected stocks are excluded. It only prepares the next input universe.
5. Configure the next rules **without `universe`**, read the new draft revision,
   then explicitly `screening.run`. An explicit replacement universe starts
   an independent comparison instead. The backend receives only ordinary
   current stocks/rules, never prior results or server pipeline metadata.

Earlier columns remain joined by unique canonical ticker. Capped results
represent returned stocks only, not every market match. Aggregate/repeated
SQL rows cannot silently refine into a stock universe. The combined sequence
is tab-only; individual history snapshots persist separately.

After `ANALYSIS_CONFLICT` or `REVISION_CONFLICT`, rediscover and reconsider the
user's current state; never blindly retry a mutation. Expanded analysis is a
real modal; close it with `setAnalysis` (`expanded:false`) before showing setup.

### Read original rows, selected stocks or an export

`screening.getResults` pages the current run's original returned rows; it does
not apply the grid's filters or join earlier refinement stages.
`screening.getAnalysis` pages the current filtered/sorted, joined grid.
For a user-requested report/export, traverse the appropriate row pagination
and, for analysis values, column pagination. Keep the same run and analysis
revision across reads; if the user changes the grid, reread rather than mixing
different snapshots. There is no dedicated `screening.export` command.

To save the visible filtered selection as a cloud watchlist, collect canonical
`ticker` values from analysis `rows` whose `selected` is true across **all row
pages**, deduplicate, then use `watchlists.create` or `watchlists.addSymbols` ([tl-markets](../tl-markets/SKILL.md))
with explicit `symbols`. Do not rely on `selectedTickers` alone: that response
list is capped at 100 and `selectionTruncated` reports the omission. Selection
arrays replace rather than append, so splitting `setAnalysis` calls is not a
way to accumulate a larger selection. Honor the addressed runtime's limits.
Cloud watchlist writes accept at most 500 explicit symbols per command; do not
silently drop excess selected stocks or split writes without reviewing scope.

### Scanned History, drafts and cache

Saved **screeners** are reusable rules; saved **scans** are executed snapshots.
`screening.listHistory` lists bounded metadata, not complete results.
`screening.show` with `view:"history"` opens the visible list; `view:"scanner"`
returns to setup. Leaving an opened historical result clears its comparison.

Use `screening.openHistory` with a discovered ID, then `getResults` or
`getAnalysis` with its returned `runId`. Opening does not rerun, charge allowance,
or replace the draft/universe. `screening.useHistorySettings` explicitly copies
that opened snapshot's rules **and original stocks** into the draft; it requires
the current draft revision and does not run. `deleteHistory` deletes only that
snapshot, requires the applicable write grant and retry key, and is never
necessary for a demonstration.

Discover `historySupported` and backend flags first. Missing support is
`HISTORY_UNAVAILABLE`, not empty history. A storage failure leaves computed
results visible with a not-saved warning. Retention is server-advertised.
Local draft restoration preserves unfinished setup independently of history;
it never executes or creates a saved screener.

Cloud presets/custom/SQL default to `cacheMode:"refresh"`; optional
`"prefer_cache"` requires advertised support and may reuse an exact request
under 60 seconds old. Hits still consume allowance. Classic is refresh-only.
Neither recalculation nor a cache timestamp proves underlying market freshness.

### Save, load and reuse

`screening.listSaved` refreshes account-owned metadata and etags; paginate it.
`screening.load` takes an ID and the current draft revision. It updates the
visible **Saved screener** dropdown and rule editor, retains the current input
list, and does not run. The same saved rules can therefore scan a different
watchlist, flag list, category or explicit stock selection.

`screening.save` persists the current visible definition with a name, optional
description and `expectedRevision`. Omit `id` to create a new screener/copy;
an update requires both its `id` and current `etag`. `screening.delete` requires
`id` and `etag`, leaves the visible draft intact, and deletes only that account's
record. Both require a retry key and the user's **Allow AI watchlist and
saved-screener changes** grant. Never enable that grant programmatically.
Inspect `persisted:true`; after a conflict refresh instead of overwriting.
An uncertain timed-out save must be inspected in the original account before
retrying, especially after a tab reload (retry receipts are session-local).

### Backend scan

Discover actual screener names/parameters. Supply 1-500 canonical tickers and
1-5 supported screener configurations. Source is the backend `default` surface,
not a guessed broker ID. Poll `screener.getResults` using the returned run ID.
Its successful terminal job status is `done`, not the visible Scanner's
`completed`; inspect its `matchedSymbols` and per-stock errors.

The public backend scan now uses the authenticated, plan-limited screening
path and reads current stored candles. `refreshCache` is only a compatibility
parameter, not proof of fresh market data. Legacy `screener.*` job handles remain
separate from the visible Scanner; use `screening.*` with `mode:"classic"` for
original strategies in the visible comparison workflow.

### Provider scan

Discover supported providers/intervals and supply 1-50 explicit canonical
tickers, the provider, TLScript-Pine **indicator** source, interval and a
supported condition.
Read [tl-tlscript](../tl-tlscript/SKILL.md) before authoring. Bars are bounded
to 2-1000. The newest candle is conservatively excluded; broker requests
consume quota. Secondary-data requests and Pine strategies are not supported
on this scan surface. Poll `providerScreener.getResults`.
Its terminal statuses are `completed` or `completed_with_errors`; inspect each
row even after an `ok` command response. Conditions use a finite numeric
`value` within ±1e9. `plotIndex` selects a real numeric output, not an arbitrary
plot inferred from a compiled script.

There is no silent provider/SQL fallback. Local runs expire after 30 minutes
or reload; an expired job is not an empty successful result.

## Inspect before saving

Check terminal status, each symbol's errors, source timestamps, missing values,
partial failures and truncation. A failed symbol is not a valid non-match.
Use the matching `cancel` command when requested; cancellation may not undo a
backend computation already dispatched.

Saving results to a cloud watchlist is owned by
[tl-markets](../tl-markets/SKILL.md): pass verified explicit `symbols` (or a
completed legacy `screener.run` job's `runId`) to `watchlists.create` or
`watchlists.addSymbols` there, with its sign-in and cloud-write rules.

To chart results as cards, use `grid.open` from
[tl-charts](../tl-charts/layouts-grid.md): `{"runId": ...}` for a completed
visible run (all result tickers in result order, deduplicated, about 1025 rows
maximum, `truncated` flag). Add `"scope":"filtered"` or `"scope":"selected"` to
chart only the rows that survive the results grid's current filters, or the
selected ones among them (`ANALYSIS_CHANGED` if the grid changes mid-read;
`NO_SYMBOLS` if none qualify). Explicit `symbols` (max 500) remain available.
This only reads screening state; it does not change the run, draft or grid
analysis.

Open a verified result via [tl-charts](../tl-charts/SKILL.md), or save its
analysis with [tl-research](../tl-research/SKILL.md). Do not invent a match for
unsupported fundamentals, conditions, datasets or indicators.

Use the scanner analysis/selection commands only for the visible Scanner result
grid; they do not manage the Watch grid, watchlists or the market heatmap (see
[tl-markets](../tl-markets/SKILL.md)). User sign-in, provider connection and
cloud-write approval remain intentional user-only boundaries; do not use
arbitrary JavaScript to fake missing commands.
